Verified by execution: `save_espnet_config("espnet2.tasks.asr.ASRTask", OmegaConf.create({"model": None, "dataset": None}), "out.yaml")` raises `TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not iterable`.
findings.suggested_fix: Check `if model_config is None: raise ValueError("training_config.model must be set when `task` is set")` before the `_target_` lookup.

findings.summary: test_get_task_class_returns_correct_class's optional-dependency skip guard only matches a 'numpy.dtype size changed' message, so in this review environment (pkg_resources/setuptools not installed) the gan_svs and svs parametrize cases fail outright rather than skip, exactly reproducing the 2 known suite failures.
findings.scenario: In an environment without pkg_resources installed (setuptools not preinstalled, as in this review env), get_class("espnet2.tasks.gan_svs.GANSVSTask") and get_class("espnet2.tasks.svs.SVSTask") fail with ModuleNotFoundError('pkg_resources'), wrapped by get_task_class into a RuntimeError; the test's `except RuntimeError as e: if "numpy.dtype size changed" in str(e): pytest.skip(...)` does not match this message, so `raise` re-raises and the test fails -- confirmed as exactly the 2 failures in review_log/pytest_espnet3.txt:390-391.
findings.evidence: test_task_utils.py:59-64 (narrow message match); review_log/pytest_espnet3.txt:98-100 `RuntimeError: Failed to get task class from espnet2.tasks.gan_svs.GANSVSTask: ... ModuleNotFoundError("No module named 'pkg_resources'")`.
findings.suggested_fix: Broaden the skip condition to also catch missing-optional-dependency ModuleNotFoundErrors (e.g. match on 'No module named' generically, or use pytest.mark.skipif keyed off whether pkg_resources/setuptools is importable).

findings.summary: _has_exp_identity detects an unresolved `${exp_tag}` in exp_dir by checking for the literal substring "None", which can false-positive on a legitimate exp_dir/exp_tag that happens to contain that text.
findings.scenario: A standalone inference_config with `exp_tag: "None_aug_v2"` produces `exp_dir = "./exp/None_aug_v2"`; `_has_exp_identity` returns False (because `"None" in exp_dir`) even though exp_tag is well-defined, so validate_experiment_context raises `ValueError: infer stage requires --training_config or a standalone inference_config with exp_tag/exp_dir.` for a config that is actually valid.
findings.evidence: run_utils.py:79-82: `return "${exp_tag}" not in exp_dir and "None" not in exp_dir`.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the `"None" not in exp_dir` substring check (the `${exp_tag}` marker check already catches the unresolved-interpolation case at this pre-resolve point in the pipeline).

findings.summary: _process_dict_config_entry assumes every `defaults:` dict entry's value is a string (`"/" not in val`), so a non-string value (e.g. a bool or nested mapping) raises a raw TypeError instead of a clear validation error; currently unreachable because no real egs3 recipe uses `defaults:` at all.
findings.scenario: A hypothetical config with `defaults: [{some_flag: true}]` would hit `"/" not in val` with `val=True`, raising `TypeError: argument of type 'bool' is not iterable` instead of an actionable message. grep over all egs3/**/*.yaml found no `defaults:` key in any real TEMPLATE/mini_an4/librispeech_100 config, so this path is exercised only by test/espnet3/utils/test_config.py today.
findings.evidence: config_utils.py:173: `composed = f"{key}/{val}" if "/" not in val else val`.
findings.suggested_fix: Coerce/validate `val` to str with a clear error message before the membership check.

findings.summary: Distributed mode is detected by `num_device > 1` (per-node device count), so multi-node DDP with one GPU per node is treated as world_size=1/rank=0: iter-factory batches are not split across ranks and shard selection is rank-independent.
findings.scenario: TEMPLATE training.yaml with num_device: 1, num_nodes: 2 (trainer.devices=${num_device}, num_nodes=${num_nodes}) and the default SequenceIterFactory path -> `_build_iter_factory` skips `batches[rank::world_size]` (line 258 `if self.num_device > 1`), every rank iterates the full batch list in identical order; EpochSyncIterator (which correctly uses torch.distributed.is_initialized()) keeps them in lock-step, so training runs with no data parallelism at N x cost and no error. With a ShardedDataset, a correctly configured dist_world_size: 2 is rejected with the misleading 'dist_world_size must match the distributed world_size (configured 2, got 1)'.
findings.evidence: dataloader.py:84-89 `if self.num_device > 1: world_size = torch.distributed.get_world_size() ... else: world_size = 1; rank = 0`; :258 `if self.num_device > 1:` guards the rank split; lightning_module.py:1138 `num_device=self.config.num_device`; egs3/TEMPLATE/asr/conf/training.yaml:17-18,263-264 num_device/num_nodes -> trainer.devices/num_nodes; iterator.py:123-124 uses is_available()/is_initialized() instead.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive rank/world_size from torch.distributed.is_initialized() (as iterator.py does) or from the Lightning trainer (self.trainer.world_size/global_rank), never from num_device.

findings.summary: collect_stats re-runs silently reuse stale per-shard outputs: CollectStatsRunner inherits BaseRunner resume=True, the manifest only fingerprints the index plan, and completed shards are skipped and re-merged regardless of model/frontend/dataset-content changes.
findings.scenario: Run collect_stats, then change the frontend (n_mels, hop_length, fs) or dataset contents while the split length and batch_size stay the same, and re-run collect_stats: manifest.json matches, split.0/done exists -> no shard is executed and merge() rewrites train/feats_stats.npz and train/feats_shape from the OLD split.0 files (even if the user deleted the top-level npz). GlobalMVN (librispeech config normalize_conf.stats_file: ${stats_dir}/train/feats_stats.npz) then normalizes with wrong statistics (crash only if the feature dim changed). TEMPLATE stats_dir=${recipe_dir}/exp/stats is shared by every experiment in a recipe (mini_an4 configs inherit it), so e.g. training_asr_streaming.yaml (raw-waveform feats) run after training_asr_transformer.yaml gets the transformer's fbank shape files.
findings.evidence: collect_stats.py:499-504 `CollectStatsRunner(provider, output_dir=output_dir, mode=mode, write_collected_feats=...)` (no resume); base_runner.py:84 `resume: bool = True`, :313-334 manifest compared only against planned index chunks, :345-346 `if self.resume and self.is_shard_done(shard_dir): continue`, :480 `return self.merge(self._get_completed_shard_dirs(shards))`; training.yaml:29 `stats_dir: ${recipe_dir}/exp/stats`. Verified: second run with DummyModel(scale=2.0) reproduced run-1 sums exactly (stale reuse: True).
findings.suggested_fix: Pass resume=False (or clear output_dir/mode) from collect_stats, or include a fingerprint of model_config/dataset_config in the manifest and refuse to resume on mismatch; consider scoping stats_dir per experiment or per frontend config.

findings.summary: A ShardedDataset used with the standard PyTorch DataLoader under Lightning DDP is sharded twice: the builder picks a rank-specific shard, then Lightning (use_distributed_sampler stays True because is_espnet_sampler is False) wraps the loader in DistributedSampler, so each rank sees only 1/world_size of its own shard.
findings.scenario: dataset with total_shards=4, dist_world_size=2, dataloader.train.iter_factory: null, num_device: 2 -> rank r gets shard (2*epoch+r)%4 (line 140) and Lightning's DistributedSampler(num_replicas=2, rank=r) then subsamples that shard -> half of every shard is never trained on in a given epoch and the two halves visited differ by rank; no error is raised. The iter_factory path cannot be used with rotating shards (shape files are global), so this is the only usable sharding path.
findings.evidence: dataloader.py:140-141 `shard_idx = ((self.epoch * runtime_world_size) + rank) % total_shards; return dataset.shard(shard_idx)`; :238-244 plain `torch.utils.data.DataLoader(dataset, sampler=None, batch_sampler=None, ...)`; trainer.py:130-131 `if self.model.is_espnet_sampler: self.config.use_distributed_sampler = False` (only then); lightning_module.py:199 is_espnet_sampler=is_train_espnet.
findings.suggested_fix: Set use_distributed_sampler=False whenever the dataset is sharded (or always, since the builder owns rank handling), and document that the standard-loader shard path expects equal shard sizes or wrap it in EpochSyncIterator to avoid unequal per-rank batch counts.

findings.summary: `total_shards`/`dist_world_size` are read from the dataset object, never from config, yet TEMPLATE/asr and mini_an4 streaming configs put them under dataloader.train/valid; the keys are dead there and crash the documented standard-DataLoader mode.
findings.scenario: TEMPLATE training.yaml (dataloader.train.total_shards: 1, dist_world_size: 1) with `iter_factory: null` + batch_size (docstring 'Case 2') -> `_build_standard_dataloader` forwards `**config` -> TypeError: DataLoader.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'total_shards' (verified). A user setting dataloader.train.total_shards: 4 to enable sharding gets no sharding at all.
findings.evidence: dataloader.py:109-110 `first_dataset = dataset.datasets[0]; total_shards = getattr(first_dataset, 'total_shards', None)`; :119 `getattr(first_dataset, 'dist_world_size', None)`; :234-243 only pops 'dataset' and 'iter_factory' before `**config`; training.yaml:223-227,243-245 and egs3/mini_an4/asr/conf/training_asr_streaming.yaml:126-129 define the keys under dataloader.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the keys from the templates (or read them from config and forward to the dataset), and whitelist/strip non-DataLoader keys before `**config`.

findings.summary: DDP tail-batch dropping removes the same `total % world_size` batches every epoch (the batch list from build_batch_sampler is deterministic; SequenceIterFactory only permutes order), so those utterances are never trained on; when total < world_size every rank gets an empty epoch.
findings.scenario: type: sorted or numel with world_size 4 and 1001 batches -> the last batch (the longest or shortest utterances, since batches are length-sorted) is dropped in every epoch of training; espnet2 instead splits inside each batch. A tiny dataset producing 1 batch with world_size 2 -> keep=0 -> `build_iter` over [] -> zero training steps with only a warning.
findings.evidence: dataloader.py:263-277 `remainder = total_batches % world_size ... batches = batches[:keep]`; :288 `batches = batches[rank::world_size]`; espnet2/iterators/sequence_iter_factory.py:75-87 shuffles the batch order per epoch only.
findings.suggested_fix: Rotate which batches are dropped per epoch (e.g. offset by epoch), or pad by repeating batches instead of dropping, and raise when keep == 0.

findings.summary: build('valid') applies the same epoch-rotating shard selection as train, so validation runs on a different shard each epoch and valid/loss values across epochs (used by best_model_criterion) are not comparable.
findings.scenario: ShardedDataset valid split with total_shards=4, world_size=1 -> epoch 0 validates shard 0, epoch 1 shard 1, ...; the min-valid/loss checkpoint selection picks whichever shard happened to be easiest.
findings.evidence: dataloader.py:195 `dataset = self._maybe_shard_dataset(self.dataset)` unconditionally for both modes; :140 shard_idx depends on self.epoch; lightning_module.py:1143-1160 val_dataloader passes epoch=self.current_epoch; training.yaml:194-197 best_model_criterion valid/loss.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not rotate valid shards by epoch (use rank only, or concatenate all shards for validation).

findings.summary: Sharding is incompatible with the iter_factory path: batches come from global shape files whose uids are CombinedDataset global indices, but the iter factory indexes the epoch/rank shard, so uids resolve to different utterances (or IndexError) after `dataset.shard()`.
findings.scenario: ShardedDataset + SequenceIterFactory with shape_files from collect_stats over the unsharded dataset: uid '57' (row 57 of the full dataset) is looked up on the shard -> CombinedDataset int-mode returns the shard's 57th item (a different utterance, wrong length for batch_bins) or raises 'Index out of range in CombinedDataset' when the shard is shorter. The error message at 199-201 suggests pointing shape files to split.*, which cannot follow the per-epoch rotation.
findings.evidence: dataloader.py:256 `batches = build_batch_sampler(**factory_config.pop('batches'))` (global shape_files) then :301 `instantiate(factory_config, dataset, batches=batches)` with the sharded dataset; dataset.py:186-193 str->int index, :212-213 `return str(idx), transformed`; collect_stats writes shape files keyed by these indices (collect_stats.py:96).
findings.suggested_fix: Reject total_shards>1 together with iter_factory, or key shape files by stable utterance ids and filter batches to the shard's keys.

findings.summary: Shape files are keyed by CombinedDataset global integer indices (uid=str(idx)), so any change in dataset composition/order between collect_stats and train silently re-maps shape entries to other utterances; nothing fingerprints the dataset.
findings.scenario: collect_stats with dataset.train = [A]; later add entry B before A (or the recipe Dataset returns rows in a different order) and run train without re-running collect_stats (the stage is considered done because stats_dir exists) -> batch_bins/sorted batching uses A's lengths for B's rows; no error.
findings.evidence: collect_stats.py:96 `shape_info[feat_key][uid] = ...` with uid from the collate output; dataset.py:212-213 `if self.use_espnet_collator: return str(idx), transformed` (global index); training.yaml:236-237 shape_files: ${stats_dir}/train/feats_shape.
findings.suggested_fix: Use stable utterance ids from the recipe dataset when available and store a dataset fingerprint (length + entry list hash) next to the shape files, checked by DataLoaderBuilder.

findings.summary: The collect_stats stage builds a full ESPnetLightningModule and ESPnet3LightningTrainer (model + DataOrganizer + loggers/callbacks) only to call model.collect_stats(), which re-instantiates the organizer and model again per split: the organizer is built 5 times and the model 3 times.
findings.scenario: TEMPLATE `--stages collect_stats`: lightning_module.py:164 instantiate(config.dataset) [1], _instantiate_model [1]; per mode: collect_stats.py:487 _get_dataset_length -> _instantiate_dataset [+1], build_env_local -> _build_dataset [+1] and _build_model [+1]. For datasets that scan manifests/HF hubs or preprocessors that load tokenizers this multiplies stage start-up time and any import-time side effects (see dataset_module local-module re-exec), and the Trainer constructor's logger/callback setup touches exp_dir for a stage that only needs stats_dir.
findings.evidence: training.py:67-68 `trainer = _build_trainer(config); trainer.collect_stats()`; trainer.py:271-279 delegates to model.collect_stats(); lightning_module.py:1189-1203 loops modes calling collect_stats(); collect_stats.py:121-131,173-181,245,256.
findings.suggested_fix: Call espnet3.components.data.collect_stats.collect_stats directly from training.collect_stats with the resolved configs, or build the dataset/model once and pass instances.

findings.summary: `data_src_args: null` (the natural YAML for 'no constructor args') raises TypeError "'NoneType' object is not iterable" from dict(None); the docstring promises ValueError.
findings.scenario: dataset.train: [{data_src: mini_an4/asr, data_src_args: }] -> plain.get('data_src_args', {}) returns None -> dict(None) -> TypeError with no mention of data_src_args (verified).
findings.evidence: dataset_module.py:207 `data_src_args = dict(plain.get(_DATA_SRC_ARGS_KEY, {}))`; docstring 184-186 'ValueError: If data_src_args is incompatible with dict(...)'.

findings.summary: The `use_parallel=True` parametrisation uses parallel env 'local', for which BaseRunner plans exactly one shard and runs on the driver, so the multi-shard merge/concatenation, the Dask path, and re-run/resume behaviour of collect_stats are never exercised; no test uses a real CombinedDataset.
findings.scenario: base_runner.py:288-289 `if par_config is not None and env not in ('local',): num_shards = n_workers` -> make_parallel_cfg(env='local', n_workers=2) yields 1 shard; __call__:475 routes env=='local' to _run_local. Regressions in CollectStatsRunner.merge ordering, concatenate_shard_files, or the stale-resume behaviour (finding above) pass these tests; the DummyDataset carries an explicit use_espnet_preprocessor attribute so the CombinedDataset tuple/dict mismatch (known) is masked.
findings.evidence: test_collect_stats.py:209-211 make_parallel_cfg returns env 'local'; :235,:365,:414 parametrize use_parallel; no test writes to an existing output_dir twice.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test with a non-local env stub (or call CollectStatsRunner._run_local over a 2-shard plan) asserting merged shape-file order and totals, a re-run test asserting recomputation, and a DataOrganizer-based test.

findings.summary: A mode config without an `iter_factory` key at all fails with ConfigAttributeError 'Missing key iter_factory' (and pop KeyError); only an explicit `iter_factory: null` selects the standard DataLoader.
findings.scenario: dataloader: {train: {batch_size: 4, shuffle: true}, valid: {...}} -> lightning_module __init__ accepts it (hasattr False) but builder.build('train') raises 'Missing key iter_factory' (verified); the same happens for build(mode) with an unknown mode because getattr defaults to an empty DictConfig.
findings.evidence: dataloader.py:192 `getattr(self.config.dataloader, mode, DictConfig({}))`; :204 `if config.iter_factory is not None`; :237 `config.pop('iter_factory')`.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `config.get('iter_factory')` / `pop('iter_factory', None)` and validate mode in {'train','valid'} as the docstring claims.

findings.summary: build() docstring claims ValueError for modes other than train/valid but nothing validates mode; and `mode` is never forwarded to _build_iter_factory/_build_standard_dataloader, so the valid loader is logged as '[train]' and, because logging is deduplicated by label, never logged at all.
findings.scenario: val_dataloader() -> build('valid') -> _build_iter_factory(factory_config, dataset) with default mode='train' -> the '[train] Dropping N tail batches' warning is emitted for the valid split and log_dataloader(label='train') is skipped after the train loader was logged.
findings.evidence: dataloader.py:216 `return self._build_iter_factory(factory_config, dataset)`; :217 `return self._build_standard_dataloader(config, dataset)`; :219,:252 `mode='train'` defaults; :22-24 and :289 dedupe on label/mode.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass mode=mode in both calls; validate mode.

findings.summary: Per-batch and cross-batch sum/sum_square accumulators stay float32 (model outputs are float32 and defaultdict(float)+float32 array remains float32), so dataset-scale sums lose precision and var = E[x^2]-E[x]^2 amplifies the error; espnet2 shares this behaviour.
findings.scenario: ~36M frames (librispeech_100) with log-mel values ~1e1 -> sum_square ~1e10 accumulated in float32 with per-add rounding ~ulp/2 ~ 6e2; verified that adding 1000 ones to 2**24 in float32 yields 0. Resulting GlobalMVN variance is biased at the 1e-3 relative level (not catastrophic).
findings.evidence: collect_stats.py:93-94 `stats[feat_key]['sum'] += seq.sum(0)` (float32 numpy); :368-369 `defaultdict(float)`; verified dtype stays float32.
findings.suggested_fix: Cast seq to float64 before summing (seq.astype(np.float64)) and accumulate in float64.

findings.summary: An empty split produces no shape or stats files and a `stats_keys` file containing only a newline; the failure surfaces much later as FileNotFoundError from build_batch_sampler on ${stats_dir}/<mode>/feats_shape.
findings.scenario: valid split resolves to 0 items (wrong split name in data_src_args) -> collect_stats returns {},{},{} silently; train stage crashes when SequenceIterFactory opens the missing valid/feats_shape.
findings.evidence: collect_stats.py:506-507 `if not index_batches: return {}, {}, {}`; :578-579 writes '\n'.join({}) + '\n'.
findings.suggested_fix: Raise (or at least log a warning) when num_items == 0.

findings.summary: Shape files are written only for collect_feats outputs and also for `*_lengths` keys, unlike espnet2 which writes shape files for every input key (speech_shape, text_shape) and skips *_lengths; espnet2 configs listing text_shape cannot be ported.
findings.scenario: Porting an espnet2 config with `shape_files: [train/speech_shape, train/text_shape]` (needed for length/numel batching on text) -> text_shape is never produced -> FileNotFoundError at train; meanwhile feats_lengths_shape and feats_lengths_stats.npz are emitted (verified in output listing).
findings.evidence: collect_stats.py:86-96 loops over `feats.keys()` including `mel_lengths`; espnet2/main_funcs/collect_stats.py:55-62 iterates `batch` keys and `if name.endswith('_lengths'): continue`.
findings.suggested_fix: Also write shape files for the collated input keys and skip *_lengths, matching espnet2.

findings.summary: The local recipe dataset module is re-executed and sys.modules overwritten on every load_dataset_module(None, recipe_dir) call, so module-level side effects repeat and each call yields distinct class objects.
findings.scenario: DataOrganizer calls instantiate_dataset_reference per entry and the collect_stats stage instantiates the organizer 5 times -> dataset/__init__.py runs >=10 times; a module-level download/manifest scan repeats and `isinstance(ds, module.Dataset)` across loads is False.
findings.evidence: dataset_module.py:103-115 builds `module_name`, `sys.modules[module_name] = module; spec.loader.exec_module(module)` unconditionally.
findings.suggested_fix: Return sys.modules[module_name] when already present.

findings.summary: resolve_dataset_module_name documents hyphen->underscore normalisation as support for `my-recipe/asr`, but an egs3 directory named my-recipe is not importable, so the example cannot work; trailing slashes also produce a confusing 'egs3.x.y..dataset' import error.
findings.scenario: data_src: my-recipe/asr with egs3/my-recipe/asr/dataset -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'egs3.my_recipe'.
findings.evidence: dataset_module.py:71 `'.'.join(part.replace('-', '_') for part in ref.split('/'))`.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate tag segments as identifiers and raise a clear error.

findings.summary: _to_plain_dict uses resolve=False, so parse_dataset_reference_config/instantiate_dataset_reference called with a root-attached DictConfig pass literal '${dataset_dir}' strings to Dataset(); it only works because DataOrganizer resolves entries first.
findings.scenario: Any caller passing cfg.dataset.train[0] directly (the public API accepts DictConfig) -> Dataset(data_path='${dataset_dir}') (verified: {'p': '${dataset_dir}'} returned).
findings.evidence: dataset_module.py:35 `OmegaConf.to_container(config, resolve=False)`; data_organizer.py:436-438 resolves before calling.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve when the node has a parent, or document the precondition.

findings.summary: `mp.set_start_method('fork', force=True)` runs at import time and mutates the multiprocessing start method for the entire pytest session.
findings.scenario: Any later test in the session relying on spawn/forkserver semantics (or the default) is affected by collection order.
findings.evidence: test_collect_stats.py:20 `mp.set_start_method('fork', force=True)` at module scope.
findings.suggested_fix: Move into a fixture using mp.get_context('fork') or drop it.

findings.summary: No test covers torch.distributed initialised with num_device=1 (multi-node), a mode config lacking iter_factory, tail-drop stability across epochs, or the sharded standard-loader path under a Lightning Trainer, so the distributed findings above are invisible to the suite.
findings.scenario: All DDP tests monkeypatch get_world_size/get_rank and pass num_device=world_size; sharded tests iterate the raw DataLoader without Lightning's DistributedSampler injection.
findings.evidence: test_dataloader_builder.py:485-487,506 num_device=2 with patched world size; :621-626 sharded assignment tests build loaders directly.
findings.suggested_fix: Add cases for num_device=1 with dist initialised, epoch-stability of dropped batches, and a Trainer-level sharding test.

findings.summary: CombinedDataset.shard() builds a fresh CombinedDataset whose _use_espnet_collator is always reset to False, dropping whatever flag the pre-shard dataset had.
findings.scenario: ESPnetLightningModule.train_dataloader sets organizer.train.use_espnet_collator = True on the *unsharded* CombinedDataset (lightning_module.py ~1130) so CommonCollateFn receives (uid, sample) tuples; DataLoaderBuilder.build then calls dataset.shard(shard_idx) per worker (dataloader.py:195) for ESPnet multiple-iterator mode. shard() (dataset.py:393-398) constructs `CombinedDataset(sharded_datasets, self.transforms, self.use_espnet_preprocessor)`, which re-runs __init__ and re-sets `self._use_espnet_collator = False` at line 165 -- the True flag set by the lightning module never reaches the sharded object because shard() has no way to carry it. The sharded dataset then returns plain sample dicts instead of (uid, sample) tuples to CommonCollateFn, breaking any pipeline that relies on ESPnet-style batching (uid-keyed lengths, ESPnetIterFactory sharding) once sharding is engaged.
findings.evidence: dataset.py:165 `self._use_espnet_collator = False` (unconditional in __init__); dataset.py:393-398 `sharded_datasets = [dataset.shard(shard_idx) for dataset in self.datasets]\n        return CombinedDataset(sharded_datasets, self.transforms, self.use_espnet_preprocessor)` never forwards use_espnet_collator. Verified by execution: scratch check D (verify_organizer.py) -- 'orig flag True -> sharded flag False ; sharded[0] type: dict'.
findings.suggested_fix: Have shard() copy self.use_espnet_collator onto the new CombinedDataset after construction (e.g. `sharded = CombinedDataset(...); sharded.use_espnet_collator = self.use_espnet_collator; return sharded`), or pass it as a constructor kwarg.

findings.summary: collect_stats_batch decides whether dataset[i] returned a (uid, sample) tuple by checking dataset.use_espnet_preprocessor, but CombinedDataset only returns that tuple when use_espnet_collator is set -- a different, independently-controlled flag.
findings.scenario: TEMPLATE recipe with an empty `preprocessor:` (do_nothing, so CombinedDataset.use_espnet_preprocessor is False) plus the default CommonCollateFn expecting (uid, dict) pairs: collect_stats_batch takes the `else` branch (`uid, sample = str(i), item`), so `sample` ends up being the correct dict and collate_fn receives well-formed pairs -- but with the *reverse* combination (preprocessor is an AbsPreprocessor instance, so use_espnet_preprocessor is True, while use_espnet_collator is still False because only ESPnetLightningModule ever sets it and collect_stats runs outside that module) collect_stats_batch takes the `uid, sample = item` branch even though dataset[i] returned a plain dict, not a tuple -- unpacking a dict into two variables iterates its keys. In the TEMPLATE flow (preprocessor configured, custom/default collate) this manifests as a TypeError from within collate_fn/model.collect_feats.
findings.evidence: collect_stats.py:41-45 `if (hasattr(dataset, "use_espnet_preprocessor") and dataset.use_espnet_preprocessor): uid, sample = item` vs dataset.py:212-215/237-239/367-369 where the (uid, sample) tuple is gated on `self.use_espnet_collator`, a separate property defaulting to False and only flipped by ESPnetLightningModule (dataset.py:164 comment). Verified by execution: scratch check E -- 'collect_stats_batch FAILED: TypeError unhashable type: 'dict'' (empty-preprocessor + CommonCollateFn direction) and 'reverse case FAILED: TypeError string indices must be integers' (AbsPreprocessor + custom collate direction). test/espnet3/components/data/test_collect_stats.py's DummyDataset (lines 51-76) hard-codes `if self.use_espnet_preprocessor: return uid, {...}` in __getitem__, i.e. it encodes collect_stats_batch's assumption directly rather than mirroring CombinedDataset's real use_espnet_collator-gated contract, so the test suite cannot see this mismatch.
findings.suggested_fix: Check `getattr(dataset, 'use_espnet_collator', False)` (the flag that actually controls whether dataset[i] returns a tuple) instead of use_espnet_preprocessor, or have DataOrganizer/collect_stats explicitly set use_espnet_collator=True on the dataset before calling collect_stats_batch.

findings.summary: When preprocessor._target_ points at a factory *function* (not an AbsPreprocessor subclass), DataOrganizer's is_espnet check is False, so the train flag is never injected -- the resulting preprocessor is instantiated identically for train and valid, so valid silently runs with train=True.
findings.scenario: A shared (non-split) preprocessor config like `preprocessor: {_target_: src.preprocess.build_preprocessor, train: true, ...}` where build_preprocessor is a plain function returning an AbsPreprocessor instance (as in TEMPLATE training.yaml's documented factory-function example, conf/training.yaml:97-98 area). `_instantiate_preprocessor_from_config` builds `partial_preprocessor = instantiate(cfg, _partial_=True)`; since the target is a function, `partial_preprocessor.func` is that function, not a class, so `isinstance(partial_preprocessor.func, type)` is False and is_espnet stays False (data_organizer.py:413-417) -- the train flag from the config is used verbatim instead of being overridden per split. In `__init__`'s non-split branch (309-318), train_preprocessor is built with train_flag=True but that argument is ignored (since is_espnet is False); because train_preprocessor comes back as an AbsPreprocessor instance, valid_preprocessor is built by calling `_instantiate_preprocessor_from_config(preprocessor_cfg, False)` again -- but train_flag=False is *also* ignored for the same reason, so valid gets the exact same train value baked into the config (e.g. train: true). Both train and valid preprocessors end up with train=True, so validation runs with training-time augmentation on.
findings.evidence: data_organizer.py:413-417 `is_espnet = (hasattr(partial_preprocessor, "func") and isinstance(partial_preprocessor.func, type) and issubclass(partial_preprocessor.func, AbsPreprocessor))` is False for a factory function; 309-318 both train_preprocessor and valid_preprocessor come from `_instantiate_preprocessor_from_config(preprocessor_cfg, <flag>)` with the same preprocessor_cfg and no flag actually applied when is_espnet is False. Verified by execution: scratch check F -- 'train was_train: True | valid was_train: True'.
findings.suggested_fix: Also detect factory functions whose return annotation or a runtime probe indicates an AbsPreprocessor result (or require factory targets to accept/forward a `train` kwarg explicitly and always pass it), so train/valid get distinct train flags even when _target_ is a function rather than a class.

findings.summary: MiniAn4Builder.is_built() only checks that manifest files exist, and MiniAn4Builder.build() writes them non-atomically (direct write, no temp file + rename), so concurrent constructions of the auto-building Dataset (DDP ranks, Dask/parallel workers) can race and observe a zero-byte, mid-line-truncated, or line-boundary-truncated manifest as "already built".
findings.scenario: egs3/mini_an4/asr/dataset/dataset.py:93-97 auto-builds inside the Dataset constructor (`if not builder.is_built(...): builder.build(...)`) with no locking. If two processes/ranks construct the dataset around the same time, one may observe `manifest.tsv` after `path.open("w")` has created the file but before any rows are written -- `is_built()` (builder.py:159-161, `all((data/p).is_file() ...)`) returns True for that zero-byte file since it only checks existence -- and the reader in dataset.py's `_read_manifest` then raises `RuntimeError("Manifest is empty: ...")`. A read mid-write can also land inside a line, causing `line.split("\t", maxsplit=2)` to unpack too few fields (ValueError), or exactly at a line boundary, silently yielding a shorter dataset with no error at all.
findings.evidence: builder.py:159-161 `return all((data / p).is_file() for p in _CFG["manifest_paths"].values())` -- existence-only, no size/checksum/marker-file check; builder.py:237-242 `with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as fh: for utt_id, wav, text in entries: fh.write(...)` writes straight to the final manifest path with no atomic rename; egs3/mini_an4/asr/dataset/dataset.py:93-97 constructs/builds with no lock around the is_built/build pair. Verified by execution: scratch check M -- with a zero-byte train.tsv, `is_source_prepared: True | is_built: True` then `MiniAn4Dataset FAILED: RuntimeError Manifest is empty: ...`; a partial-line manifest gave `FAILED: ValueError not enough values to unpack (expected 3, got 2)`; a manifest truncated exactly at a line boundary gave `len: 1 (no error)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Write manifests to a temp file in the same directory and os.rename() into place atomically, and/or guard is_built()/build() with a file lock (or have only rank 0 build, with other ranks waiting on a barrier) so concurrent constructors never observe a partially written manifest.

findings.summary: In string-index (mixed) mode, sub-datasets that support integer indexing are never registered in _uid_to_dataset, so combined["<int-as-string>"] raises ValueError even though the same lookup works when every sub-dataset is int-addressable; an empty sub-dataset alone is also enough to flip the whole CombinedDataset into string mode.
findings.scenario: Combine one int-addressable dataset with one dataset that only exposes string keys. _initialize_index_mode's registration loop (271-276) does `if self._dataset_supports_int[dataset_idx]: continue`, so the int-addressable dataset's numeric positions are never added to _uid_to_dataset. `combined["0"]` then goes through `_resolve_string_mode_index` (316-353), which for a string idx only consults `_uid_to_dataset` (344-351) and raises `ValueError: Utterance ID '0' is not supported by the underlying datasets.` -- even though `combined[0]` (integer) works fine and, in a *pure* numeric-mode CombinedDataset, `combined["0"]` also works (via the int(idx) coercion in __getitem__, line 186-192). This silently breaks any caller (e.g. ESPnet iter_factory, which batches by uid strings) that treats uids as interchangeable strings across mixed datasets. Separately, any single empty sub-dataset (len 0) makes `supports_integer_index` return... actually flips mode: since an empty dataset's `dataset[0]` raises IndexError -> supports_integer_index is False for it -> `all_integer_addressable` is False -> the whole CombinedDataset (all sub-datasets, including otherwise-int-addressable ones) is forced into string mode, and any of those other datasets that expose no string keys becomes unreachable by index.
findings.evidence: dataset.py:271-276 registration loop skips int-addressable datasets; dataset.py:344-351 string-idx lookup only checks _uid_to_dataset. Verified by execution: scratch check C -- 'string mode? True', `c[0] ok -> a0` but `c['0'] FAILED: ValueError Utterance ID '0' is not supported by the underlying datasets.`, while 'pure numeric c2['0'] -> a0' succeeds; check C2 -- an empty sub-dataset alone: 'string mode with an empty dataset? True', and the previously-int-addressable dataset's numeric-string lookup then also fails (`c3['1'] FAILED: ValueError ...`).
findings.suggested_fix: In mixed mode, also register a str(position)->()dataset_idx, position) mapping for int-addressable sub-datasets during _initialize_index_mode, so numeric-string uids keep working alongside real string uids; treat an empty sub-dataset as a non-signal for mode detection rather than forcing string mode.

findings.summary: supports_integer_index() swallows every exception from dataset[0], not just IndexError, so a dataset whose first item is merely corrupt/unreadable is silently misclassified as a string-index dataset instead of surfacing the real error at construction time.
findings.scenario: A dataset that supports integer indexing but whose item 0 happens to be a corrupt file (e.g. a bad wav that raises a decoder error) is probed by `supports_integer_index` via a bare `except Exception: return False`. The dataset is then treated as string-index-only and CombinedDataset falls into `_collect_string_keys`, which for a plain indexable dataset with no `.keys()` tries `iter(dataset)` -- for a `__getitem__`-only Dataset, `iter()` falls back to repeatedly calling `__getitem__(0), __getitem__(1), ...` until IndexError, immediately re-triggering the *same* corrupt-item error, so the real exception does eventually surface, but only via a confusing detour through the string-mode machinery (TypeError about non-string keys, or the original error re-raised from an unrelated call site) rather than a clear failure at the point of the actual bad item.
findings.suggested_fix: Catch a narrower set of exceptions (e.g. IndexError, KeyError, TypeError) that genuinely indicate "not integer-addressable", and let other exceptions from dataset[0] propagate immediately so the failure is attributed to the actual bad item.

findings.summary: CombinedDataset.__repr__ references self.multiple_iterator, which is never assigned anywhere in the class, so repr(combined_dataset) always raises AttributeError.
findings.scenario: Any code path that logs or prints a CombinedDataset -- including DataOrganizer.log_summary/_log_dataset, which calls build_qualified_name(combined) and, for exceptions, standard %r logging -- can crash. Even a bare `repr(dataset)` in a debugger or an error message crashes instead of describing the dataset.
findings.evidence: dataset.py:416 `f\"multiple_iterator={self.multiple_iterator}, \"` inside __repr__ (400-419); no `self.multiple_iterator = ...` assignment exists anywhere in __init__ (82-165) or elsewhere in the class. Verified by execution: scratch check A -- 'REPR FAILED: AttributeError 'CombinedDataset' object has no attribute 'multiple_iterator''.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the multiple_iterator field from __repr__ (it appears to be leftover from an earlier design), or add and maintain the corresponding attribute if it is meant to reflect ESPnet's multiple-iterator mode.

findings.summary: In numeric mode, a negative integer index is not range-checked and falls through to Python's negative-indexing semantics on only the *first* sub-dataset, silently returning the wrong item with a misleading uid, inconsistent with string mode (which explicitly raises IndexError for negative indices).
findings.scenario: `combined[-1]` on a CombinedDataset with sub-datasets of length 2 and 2 (total 4): the loop `for i, cum_len in enumerate(self.cumulative_lengths): if idx < cum_len` matches i=0 immediately since -1 < 2, so `ds_idx = idx = -1`, and `self.datasets[0][-1]` returns dataset 0's *last* element (Python negative-index semantics) instead of raising IndexError or returning the combined dataset's actual last element (which lives in dataset 1). The returned uid is `str(idx)` = "-1", which does not correspond to any real utterance. Compare `_resolve_string_mode_index` (316-319), which explicitly raises `IndexError("Index out of range in CombinedDataset")` for any negative int -- so behavior differs by mode for the same misuse.
findings.evidence: dataset.py:194-196 `for i, cum_len in enumerate(self.cumulative_lengths): if idx < cum_len: ds_idx = idx if i == 0 else ...` has no `idx < 0` guard. Verified by execution: scratch check B -- 'len 4 c[-1] -> a1 (python semantics would give b1)', i.e. c[-1] silently returned dataset 0's tail item instead of the true last item or an error; 'c[-1] with collator -> -1 a1' shows the bogus uid "-1" attached to that wrong item.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject negative indices in __getitem__ (raise IndexError) the same way _resolve_string_mode_index already does, for consistency between the two modes.

findings.summary: _load_local_dataset_module loads recipe_dir/dataset/__init__.py via a synthetic module name every time (used whenever a dataset entry omits data_src), so the resulting Dataset class's __module__ is not a real importable path and instances are unpicklable in a fresh interpreter -- unlike the tag-reference path (data_src set) which imports the real egs3.<recipe>.<task>.dataset package.
findings.scenario: mini_an4's own recipe config omits data_src (local mode) for its dataset entries, so every DataOrganizer construction loads dataset/__init__.py through `util.spec_from_file_location` with `module_name = f"_espnet3_local_dataset_{sanitized}"`. `MiniAn4Dataset.__module__` ends up as that synthetic name (e.g. `_espnet3_local_dataset_..._py.dataset`), not `egs3.mini_an4.asr.dataset.dataset`. Any DataLoader configuration that spawns worker processes (num_workers>0 with the default/spawn start method, ddp_spawn strategy, or macOS where fork is unavailable) needs to pickle the dataset (or samples produced holding references to it) into the worker; unpickling in the fresh worker interpreter fails because `_espnet3_local_dataset_...` was never registered as a real package there. librispeech_100's dataset/__init__.py instead uses absolute imports (`from egs3.librispeech_100.asr.dataset.dataset import ...`), which resolve through the real `egs3` package rather than the synthetic loader's relative-import machinery, so its Dataset class stays picklable -- an inconsistency between the two example recipes that a new recipe author has no way to know about.
findings.evidence: dataset_module.py:102-116 constructs a fresh `module_name` per call and `exec_module`s it; egs3/mini_an4/asr/dataset/__init__.py:3-4 uses relative imports (`from .builder import ...`, `from .dataset import ...`) vs egs3/librispeech_100/asr/dataset/__init__.py:3-6 using absolute imports. Verified by execution: scratch check G -- `Dataset.__module__: _espnet3_local_dataset_..._py.dataset`, `local Dataset is egs3 package Dataset? False`, `fresh-interpreter unpickle: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named '_espnet3_local_dataset_...'`, while `librispeech Dataset.__module__: egs3.librispeech_100.asr.dataset.dataset` (a real, picklable path).
findings.suggested_fix: Prefer absolute imports inside recipe dataset/__init__.py files as documented convention (as librispeech already does), or change _load_local_dataset_module to import the real egs3.<recipe>.<task>.dataset package by path instead of a synthetic name so local and tag-referenced loading produce the same, picklable module identity.

findings.summary: When preprocessor is passed as an already-instantiated AbsPreprocessor, DataOrganizer reuses that same instance (not a copy) for valid and test and mutates its .train attribute in place, which both surprises the caller (whose object's state changes as a side effect of building the organizer) and does not rebuild train-dependent state baked in at the preprocessor's own construction time.
findings.scenario: A caller builds `pp = MiniAn4TokenizeSpeedPerturbPreprocessor(train=True, speed_perturb_prob=0.1, speed_perturb_factors=[0.95, 1.05], ...)` and passes it directly as `DataOrganizer(preprocessor=pp, ...)`. Because MiniAn4TokenizeSpeedPerturbPreprocessor.__init__ (egs3/mini_an4/asr/src/preprocessor.py:26-44) computes `data_aug_effects`/`data_aug_prob` from `train` *once* and bakes them into an inner `self._delegate = CommonPreprocessor(...)`, later setting `valid_preprocessor.train = False` (data_organizer.py:326, on the caller's own `pp` object) changes the outer `.train` flag but leaves `_delegate`'s already-built speed-perturb augmentation config untouched -- so calling the "valid" preprocessor still applies training-time speed perturbation. Separately, the caller's own `pp` object is left with `.train == False` after DataOrganizer construction even though the caller may still be holding a reference to it expecting `.train == True` (e.g. for reuse elsewhere), which is a surprising, hard-to-diagnose side effect.
findings.evidence: data_organizer.py:319-331 `elif isinstance(preprocessor_cfg, AbsPreprocessor): ... valid_preprocessor = preprocessor_cfg; valid_preprocessor.train = False ... test_preprocessor = preprocessor_cfg; test_preprocessor.train = False` -- no deepcopy for valid/test, and only .train is flipped. egs3/mini_an4/asr/src/preprocessor.py:26-44 shows train-dependent state (`data_aug_effects`, `data_aug_prob`) computed once in __init__ from the `train` argument and stored in `self._delegate`, which is never rebuilt when `.train` is later reassigned. Verified by execution: scratch check P -- "caller's pp.train after DataOrganizer: False" confirms the caller's original object was mutated.
findings.suggested_fix: Deepcopy preprocessor_cfg for valid_preprocessor and test_preprocessor as is already done for train_preprocessor, so the caller's original instance is never mutated; document that AbsPreprocessor subclasses with train-dependent internal state built in __init__ (like the delegate pattern here) are not safe to reuse this way, or have DataOrganizer re-instantiate rather than mutate.

findings.summary: A split preprocessor config that omits 'train' silently leaves the train split with no preprocessor at all (do_nothing) while valid/test still get a real preprocessor -- the code only logs a warning, and the resulting mismatched (untokenized train vs tokenized valid) configuration is never rejected.
findings.scenario: A user writes `preprocessor: {valid: {_target_: ..., ...}, token_type: bpe, ...}` and forgets a `train:` block (e.g. a copy-paste edit that keeps valid but drops train). `train_cfg` stays None (279-283 only warns), so `train_preprocessor = self._instantiate_preprocessor_from_config(None, True)` returns `do_nothing` (410-411) -- the training dataset is never tokenized/preprocessed at all, while valid (and test, via the valid fallback) *is* tokenized. Training then either crashes deep inside the model on raw text/audio-shape mismatches, or silently trains on unprocessed samples, with only a log line (easy to miss in a long stdout) indicating why.
findings.evidence: data_organizer.py:279-283 `if train_cfg is None: logger.warning("Split preprocessor config is missing 'train'. The train split will not use a preprocessor.")` -- warning only, no exception; data_organizer.py:410-411 `if preprocessor_cfg is None: return do_nothing`. Verified by execution: scratch check Q -- 'train sample keys: ['speech', 'text'] | valid sample keys: ['speech', 'text', 'token_list', 'was_train']' and 'train use_espnet_preprocessor: False | valid: True', confirming train is silently left untokenized while valid is not.
findings.suggested_fix: Raise instead of warn when a split config defines valid/test but omits train (or vice versa for the documented fallback chain), since a downstream shape/type crash or silent under-preprocessing is a much worse failure mode than an upfront config error.

findings.summary: parse_dataset_reference_config's docstring documents ValueError for an incompatible data_src_args, but `data_src_args: null` (a real, easy-to-write YAML value) actually raises TypeError; the one existing test named for this case asserts ValueError but exercises a different (string) input, leaving the documented/None case untested.
findings.scenario: A recipe author writes `data_src_args:` with no value (YAML null) intending "no extra args", expecting the documented default-empty-dict behavior. `plain.get(_DATA_SRC_ARGS_KEY, {})` at line 207 returns the *actual* value None (since the key is present), so `dict(None)` raises `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable` -- not the ValueError the docstring promises (lines 184-187 'Raises: ... ValueError: If data_src_args is incompatible with dict(...)'). test_dataset_module.py's `test_instantiate_dataset_reference_invalid_kwargs_raises_type_error` (despite its name) passes `{"data_src_args": "not-a-mapping"}` (a string) and asserts `pytest.raises(ValueError)` -- `dict("not-a-mapping")` does raise ValueError, so that test passes, but it neither tests the TypeError its own name implies nor the null/None case that actually produces one.
findings.evidence: dataset_module.py:207 `data_src_args = dict(plain.get(_DATA_SRC_ARGS_KEY, {}))`; dataset_module.py:184-187 docstring says `ValueError: If data_src_args is incompatible with dict(...)`. Verified by execution: scratch check H -- `data_src_args: null` gives `FAILED: TypeError 'NoneType' object is not iterable`; test/espnet3/utils/test_dataset_module.py:249-257 test named `..._raises_type_error` does `with pytest.raises(ValueError): dm.instantiate_dataset_reference({"data_src_args": "not-a-mapping"}, ...)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat an explicit null the same as an omitted key (`plain.get(_DATA_SRC_ARGS_KEY) or {}`), update the docstring to mention TypeError as well as ValueError depending on the bad value's type, and rename/extend the existing test to cover the null case explicitly.

findings.summary: DatasetConfig is advertised in DataOrganizer's own type hints and docstring examples as an accepted per-entry config type, but passing an actual DatasetConfig instance crashes with TypeError deep inside dataset_module.py, and the DataOrganizer.__init__ preprocessor type hint (Callable[[dict], dict]) does not match the documented (uid, sample) calling convention.
findings.scenario: A user follows the DatasetConfig docstring example (data_organizer.py:42-54) and passes `train=[DatasetConfig(name="custom", data_src="mini_an4/asr", data_src_args={...})]` to DataOrganizer, matching the declared type `Optional[List[Union[DatasetConfig, Dict[str, Any], DictConfig]]]` (line 246). `_build_dataset_list` treats non-DictConfig entries as already-dict-like (`raw_config = config`) and calls `instantiate_dataset_reference(raw_config, ...)`, which calls `parse_dataset_reference_config` -> `_to_plain_dict` -> `dict(config)` on the DatasetConfig dataclass instance, raising TypeError because a dataclass instance is not iterable as key/value pairs. Separately, the `preprocessor: Optional[Callable[[dict], dict]] = None` hint at line 249 describes a single-argument callable, but the documented/implemented AbsPreprocessor convention calls `preprocessor(uid, sample)` (two positional args) whenever use_espnet_preprocessor is True -- the type hint does not describe the actual calling contract.
findings.evidence: data_organizer.py:23-69 defines DatasetConfig as a dataclass and documents it as directly usable; data_organizer.py:246,249 declare the Union/Callable hints; dataset_module.py:31-36 `_to_plain_dict`: `return dict(config)` for a non-DictConfig input. Verified by execution: scratch check K -- `DatasetConfig instance ... FAILED: TypeError 'DatasetConfig' object is not iterable`.
findings.suggested_fix: Either make DatasetConfig actually usable (convert it via dataclasses.asdict() before treating a config entry as a mapping) or remove it and the misleading docstring examples/type hints entirely if it is meant to be replaced by plain dict/DictConfig entries; fix the preprocessor type hint to reflect the real (uid, sample) vs (sample) dual calling convention.

findings.summary: LibriSpeech100Dataset's class docstring documents that dataset[0] returns a sample with an 'utt_id' key, but __getitem__ only ever returns 'speech' and 'text' -- utt_id is silently absent, and a downstream helper relies on the documented-but-missing key.
findings.scenario: Anyone relying on the docstring (`>>> sorted(sample.keys())` -> `['speech', 'text', 'utt_id']`) to identify the current utterance, e.g. for logging or output keying, gets a KeyError, or (as in this recipe's own src/inference.py) silently falls back to a positional index instead. `egs3/librispeech_100/asr/src/inference.py:6` does `utt_id = data.get("utt_id", str(idx))`, so with the real dataset every inference output is keyed by the numeric dataloader index rather than the true LibriSpeech utterance id, making SCP files (hyp/ref keyed by 'utt_id') impossible to align with the original corpus IDs and fragile under any reordering (e.g. shuffled DataLoader, sharding, or DDP) since the index no longer corresponds to a stable utterance identity.
findings.evidence: egs3/librispeech_100/asr/dataset/dataset.py:90-94 docstring example claims `['speech', 'text', 'utt_id']`; dataset.py:134-140 `__getitem__` returns only `{"speech": ..., "text": ...}`; egs3/librispeech_100/asr/src/inference.py:6 `utt_id = data.get("utt_id", str(idx))` falls back to str(idx).
findings.suggested_fix: Either add 'utt_id': example.utt_id to the returned sample dict (matching the docstring and the mini_an4 recipe convention) or fix the docstring to match actual behavior and make src/inference.py fail loudly instead of silently keying by index.

findings.summary: build() checks `if not wav.exists()` before invoking sph2pipe, but the wav file is created (via `wav.open("wb")`) before the subprocess runs into it, so an interrupted/killed sph2pipe run leaves a zero-byte or partial wav that a subsequent build() call will treat as already converted and skip re-conversion.
findings.scenario: build() is interrupted (OOM kill, SIGTERM, disk full, or a race with another concurrent build() call per finding #4) partway through converting one utterance's .sph to .wav. The partially-written wav file already exists on disk. On the next run, `if not wav.exists()` (line 218) is False for that file, so sph2pipe is never re-invoked; the corrupt/truncated wav is written into the manifest as-is and later fails (or silently mis-decodes) when read by soundfile in MiniAn4Dataset.__getitem__.
findings.evidence:
builder.py:216-224 `wav = (data / "wav" / split / f"{utt_id}.wav").resolve()
                wav.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                if not wav.exists():
                    with wav.open("wb") as fh:
                        subprocess.run([sph2pipe, ...], stdout=fh, check=True)` -- the file is created by open("wb") immediately, before conversion completes, so existence alone is not a valid "conversion succeeded" signal. (analytic: not exercised via a scratch script, reasoned from the code structure and the confirmed non-atomic-write pattern already verified for manifests in finding #4.)
findings.suggested_fix: Write to a temporary path and rename to the final .wav path only after subprocess.run succeeds (matching the fix suggested for the manifest-writing race in finding #4), so a half-converted file is never mistaken for a finished one.

findings.summary: _scan_split silently skips any transcript line with no words after the utt_id or whose corresponding .flac file is missing, so a corpus with a few bad/missing files produces a silently smaller split instead of surfacing the problem.
findings.scenario: If the LibriSpeech download/extraction is incomplete (a handful of missing .flac files) or a transcript line is malformed (empty transcript after the utt_id), `_scan_split` just `continue`s past that line (54-55, 57-58) without logging or counting skips. The dataset ends up with fewer examples than the true corpus, with no signal to the user beyond a smaller-than-expected `len(dataset)` -- easy to miss, and indistinguishable from a correctly-smaller subset/debug split.
findings.suggested_fix: Log a warning (with a count) for skipped lines/missing audio at the end of _scan_split, or raise if the skip rate exceeds a small threshold, so silent corpus truncation is visible.

findings.summary: Test dataset entries with neither an explicit 'name' nor a 'data_src' all collapse to the same key ("local"), so multiple unnamed local test sets silently overwrite each other in self.test_sets and only the last one survives.
findings.scenario: A recipe defines `test: [{data_src_args: {split: a}}, {data_src_args: {split: b}}]` (two local test datasets, neither with a `name` or `data_src`). `name = raw_config.get("name") or str(raw_config.get("data_src") or "local")` evaluates to "local" for both entries, so `self.test_sets["local"] = ...` is assigned twice and the first test dataset is silently dropped -- `organizer.test` ends up with only one entry ("local") instead of two, and downstream metric/measure stages silently evaluate only the second split under a generic "local" name.
findings.evidence: data_organizer.py:392-394 `name = raw_config.get("name") or str(raw_config.get("data_src") or "local")`; the dict assignment at line 395 `self.test_sets[name] = DatasetWithTransform(...)` is a plain overwrite with no duplicate-key check. Verified by execution: scratch check R -- two unnamed test entries produced `test keys: ['fakepp']` (a single collapsed key), not two.
findings.suggested_fix: Require an explicit 'name' for any test entry lacking data_src (raise a clear error instead of collapsing to "local"), or auto-disambiguate by appending an index when multiple entries would collide.

findings.summary: resolve_dataset_module_name/load_dataset_module produce confusing module-not-found errors for common typos: an unknown recipe tag surfaces a raw 'No module named ...' with no hint that it came from a data_src typo, and a trailing slash in the tag produces a malformed module path with an empty segment.
findings.scenario: A recipe config has `data_src: mini_an4/asr/` (trailing slash, easy typo) or `data_src: nosuchrecipe/asr`. resolve_dataset_module_name splits on "/" and rejoins with ".", so a trailing slash produces a module path with a dangling empty segment (e.g. "egs3.mini_an4.asr..dataset"), and import_module raises a generic ModuleNotFoundError that does not mention data_src, the recipe tag, or that ESPnet3 resolved it via the tag convention -- a user has to know the internal `egs3.<recipe>.<task>.dataset` convention to connect the error back to their YAML typo.
findings.evidence: dataset_module.py:51-72 `resolve_dataset_module_name` does `".".join(part.replace("-", "_") for part in ref.split("/"))` with no validation that ref has no empty segments; dataset_module.py:162-168 `if _is_tag(data_src): return import_module(resolve_dataset_module_name(data_src))` lets import_module's raw error surface unmodified.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate that a tag-form data_src has no empty path segments and raise a clear error naming the offending data_src value; wrap import_module's ModuleNotFoundError to mention the original data_src and the resolved module path it produced.

findings.summary: The shipped librispeech e_branchformer tuning config sets `train: true` explicitly inside a shared (non-split) preprocessor block, which DataOrganizer always overrides -- so this recipe emits the 'will be ignored' warning on every single DataOrganizer construction (every pipeline stage).
findings.scenario: training_e_branchformer.yaml:37-49 defines one shared `preprocessor: {_target_: ...CommonPreprocessor, train: true, ...}` (no per-split train/valid/test sub-blocks). `_instantiate_preprocessor_from_config` detects `"train" in preprocessor_cfg` (data_organizer.py:419-425) and logs a warning every time this config is loaded -- i.e. at every stage of `run.py` (create_dataset, train_tokenizer, collect_stats, train, ...), cluttering logs with a warning about a value that was harmless but is not actually needed since DataOrganizer always sets train itself.
findings.evidence: egs3/librispeech_100/asr/conf/tuning/training_e_branchformer.yaml:44 `train: true` inside the shared preprocessor block; data_organizer.py:418-425 `if is_espnet: if "train" in preprocessor_cfg: logger.warning(...)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the redundant `train: true` line from the shipped tuning config (it is silently ignored anyway), so the example recipe does not itself trigger the warning it is meant to catch in user configs.

findings.summary: The TTS TEMPLATE leaves `dataset:` empty in all three conf files (training/inference/metrics) instead of demonstrating the `_target_: .../DataOrganizer` + `_recursive_: false` pattern the ASR TEMPLATE uses, so a TTS recipe author who fills it in without also adding `_recursive_: false` will have Hydra eagerly pre-instantiate the nested preprocessor/transform configs, silently routing preprocessor construction through the AbsPreprocessor-instance code path (finding #10) instead of DataOrganizer's own dict-config handling.
findings.scenario: A new TTS recipe copies `dataset: {_target_: espnet3.components.data.data_organizer.DataOrganizer, recipe_dir: ..., train: [...], valid: [...], preprocessor: {_target_: ..., train: {...}, valid: {...}}}` but, unlike the ASR TEMPLATE (conf/training.yaml:100-107), does not know to add `_recursive_: false` since the TTS TEMPLATE never shows it. Without that flag, Hydra's default recursive instantiation builds the nested `preprocessor` sub-config into a real object *before* calling `DataOrganizer.__init__`, so DataOrganizer receives an already-instantiated AbsPreprocessor rather than a dict/DictConfig -- taking the instance path (data_organizer.py:319-331) with its caller-mutation and stale-train-dependent-state issues (finding #10) instead of the intended split-preprocessor dict path (which correctly sets a fresh train flag per split at instantiation time).
findings.evidence: egs3/TEMPLATE/asr/conf/training.yaml:100-101 `_target_: espnet3.components.data.data_organizer.DataOrganizer` immediately followed by `_recursive_: false`, load-bearing for the split-preprocessor mechanism; egs3/TEMPLATE/tts/conf/training.yaml:35-36, inference.yaml:15-16, and metrics.yaml:13-14 all leave `dataset:` as a bare empty key with no _target_/_recursive_ example to copy from.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a commented-out (or minimal working) dataset: block to the TTS TEMPLATE showing _target_: DataOrganizer with _recursive_: false, matching the ASR TEMPLATE, so TTS recipe authors don't have to discover this Hydra footgun independently.

findings.summary: The split-preprocessor path always instantiates train_preprocessor even when DataOrganizer is being used inference-only (train=None), wasting work and, if the train-split preprocessor config is malformed or references training-only resources, causing an inference-only construction to fail for reasons unrelated to inference.
findings.scenario: An inference-only DataOrganizer(train=None, test=test_configs, preprocessor=<split config with train/valid/test blocks>) still executes `train_preprocessor = self._instantiate_preprocessor_from_config(train_cfg, True)` (299-301) unconditionally, even though `self.train` stays None (345 `if train is not None: ...` is skipped) and train_preprocessor is never used for anything except being stored at `self.preprocessor` (line 340). If train_cfg's _target_ needs resources only available during training (e.g. a tokenizer artifact not yet built at inference time), constructing an inference-only DataOrganizer fails even though train data was never requested.
findings.evidence: data_organizer.py:296-307 unconditionally builds train_preprocessor/valid_preprocessor/test_preprocessor from the split config regardless of whether `train` (the dataset list argument) is None; line 345 `if train is not None: self.train = self._build_dataset_list(train, train_preprocessor)` is the only consumer of train_preprocessor besides self.preprocessor.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip instantiating train_preprocessor when the `train` argument is None (mirroring the `if train is not None` guard already used for building self.train), instantiating it lazily or only when actually needed.

findings.summary: MiniAn4Builder.prepare_source() downloads the archive directly to its final path with no atomicity or completeness marker, so an interrupted download (Ctrl-C, OOM-kill, preemption, network drop) leaves a truncated downloads.tar.gz that is_source_prepared()/prepare_source() treat as already-present on the next run, and is_source_prepared() only checks directory existence afterward so a partial extraction can be reported as fully prepared forever.
findings.scenario: First `python run.py --stages create_dataset` is killed while urlretrieve(url, archive) (line 125) is mid-write. downloads.tar.gz now exists but is truncated. Re-running create_dataset: `archive.exists()` (line 120) is True, so the download is skipped; `tar -xzf` (line 130-133) either raises CalledProcessError with an unhelpful generic tar error (no message pointing at the real cause), or partially extracts an4/etc and an4/wav with some files missing before erroring. On any later invocation, `is_source_prepared()` (lines 64-90) reports True as soon as both directories exist at all -- it never re-validates completeness -- so `build()` (lines 192-242) proceeds against an incomplete source tree, either crashing deep inside the transcript loop when a referenced .sph file is missing, or (combined with the already-known sph2pipe zero-byte-wav bug) silently writing manifest rows that point at empty wav files.
findings.evidence: prepare_source(): `if not archive.exists(): ... urlretrieve(url, str(archive))` (lines 120-125) writes straight to the final path with no temp file/rename/checksum. is_source_prepared(): `return (an4/etc).is_dir() and (an4/wav).is_dir()` (line 90) is existence-only, no size/manifest check.
findings.suggested_fix: Download to a temp path in the same directory (e.g. archive.with_suffix('.tmp')) and os.replace() it into place only after the download completes successfully; optionally verify the extracted tree against a known file count or checksum before returning True from is_source_prepared().

findings.summary: The DATASET CREATION SETTING block documents a `create_dataset.func` hook ('The function is resolved from create_dataset.func and called with the remaining fields in this block as keyword arguments') that the actual create_dataset stage never reads -- BaseSystem.create_dataset() ignores `func`/`dataset_dir` entirely and instead loads the recipe's dataset/__init__.py DatasetBuilder class.
findings.scenario: A new recipe author follows the canonical TEMPLATE, writes `src/creating_dataset.py` with a `create_dataset(dataset_dir=...)` function matching the documented contract, and expects run.py --stages create_dataset to call it. It never runs: BaseSystem.create_dataset() (espnet3/systems/base/system.py:226-278) does `default_builder_kwargs = dict(create_dataset_config)` and then, per dataset entry, loads `module.DatasetBuilder()` from the recipe's dataset/__init__.py and calls is_source_prepared/prepare_source/is_built/build(**builder_kwargs) -- `func` is just an inert extra kwarg silently absorbed by the builder's **kwargs. Neither mini_an4 nor librispeech_100 (the two real recipes) ship a src/creating_dataset.py, consistent with the hook being dead everywhere in the tree.
findings.evidence: Verified by execution: loading mini_an4's real conf/training.yaml through load_and_merge_config(..., default_package='egs3.TEMPLATE.asr') yields `cfg.create_dataset == {'func': 'src.creating_dataset.create_dataset', 'dataset_dir': '/path/to/your/dataset', 'recipe_dir': '.'}` -- the TEMPLATE placeholder leaks straight into the real recipe's resolved config, unused. grep -rn 'create_dataset.func' espnet3/ finds no reader; espnet3/systems/base/system.py:239 `default_builder_kwargs = dict(create_dataset_config)` is the only consumer and it never looks at the 'func' key.
findings.suggested_fix: Either implement the documented func-hook mechanism in BaseSystem.create_dataset(), or delete the func/dataset_dir fields and the misleading comment from TEMPLATE/asr/conf/training.yaml and document the actual dataset/__init__.py:DatasetBuilder contract instead.

findings.summary: TEMPLATE/asr's readme -- the generic canonical-runner template -- opens its Quick start with a LibriSpeech-specific, factually wrong step ('Convert LibriSpeech to Hugging Face format (run once)') that matches neither TEMPLATE's own generic create_dataset mechanism nor either real recipe's actual behavior.
findings.scenario: A user copies egs3/TEMPLATE/asr as a starting point for an unrelated dataset, follows readme.md step 1 expecting a Hugging Face conversion step, but TEMPLATE's create_dataset stage does not convert anything to 'Hugging Face format' (see the create_dataset.func dead-hook finding above) and no shipped recipe does either: mini_an4 builds TSV manifests from AN4 (egs3/mini_an4/asr/dataset/builder.py), and librispeech_100's builder only validates that raw LibriSpeech directories are already present on disk (egs3/librispeech_100/asr/dataset/builder.py:85-153, prepare_source() just raises FileNotFoundError if splits are missing -- no conversion of any kind). librispeech_100/asr/readme.md itself says 'Place the corpus under download/LibriSpeech ... before running create_dataset/train' and its own Quick start skips create_dataset entirely, confirming TEMPLATE's text is stale leftover copy, not a generalized instruction.
findings.evidence: TEMPLATE/asr/readme.md:13-14: `# 1) Convert LibriSpeech to Hugging Face format (run once)\npython run.py --stages create_dataset --training_config conf/training.yaml`. Contrast with librispeech_100/asr/readme.md:1-5 ('Place the corpus under download/LibriSpeech...') and egs3/librispeech_100/asr/dataset/builder.py:108-132 (prepare_source only validates, never converts).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the LibriSpeech-specific comment in TEMPLATE/asr/readme.md with a generic placeholder describing what create_dataset does for *this* template (build/validate the recipe's dataset via dataset/__init__.py:DatasetBuilder), matching the DATASET CREATION SETTING comments already in TEMPLATE/asr/conf/training.yaml.

findings.summary: publication.yaml's exp_dir omits the ${recipe_dir} prefix that training.yaml and inference.yaml both use, so a recipe with a non-default recipe_dir gets a different exp_dir for standalone pack_model/upload_model than for train/infer.
findings.scenario: A recipe sets a non-default `recipe_dir` (e.g. runs run.py from a different cwd with recipe_dir overridden) and runs `pack_model`/`upload_model` standalone (only --publication_config, no --training_config, which the publication.yaml comments explicitly say is supported: 'Override inference_dir only when...'). training.yaml/inference.yaml resolve exp_dir as ${recipe_dir}/exp/${exp_tag}; publication.yaml resolves it as plain exp/${exp_tag} relative to CWD instead of recipe_dir, so pack_model looks for the experiment in the wrong directory when CWD != recipe_dir.
findings.evidence: egs3/TEMPLATE/asr/conf/training.yaml:28 `exp_dir: ${recipe_dir}/exp/${exp_tag}`; egs3/TEMPLATE/asr/conf/inference.yaml:23 same; egs3/TEMPLATE/asr/conf/publication.yaml:27 `exp_dir: exp/${exp_tag}` (no ${recipe_dir}).
findings.suggested_fix: Change publication.yaml line 27 to `exp_dir: ${recipe_dir}/exp/${exp_tag}` for consistency with training.yaml/inference.yaml.

findings.summary: The ~110-line Gradio launcher (build_demo/main) is duplicated verbatim across TEMPLATE/asr/src/app.py, mini_an4/asr/src/app.py, and librispeech_100/asr/src/app.py instead of living once as a shared helper that recipe-local app.py files import.
findings.scenario: Any future change to the positional input/output component wiring, error handling, or logging in the demo launcher (e.g. fixing a Gradio API change) must be manually replicated in every recipe's src/app.py; missing one leaves that recipe's packed demo silently behind or broken relative to the others.
findings.evidence: `diff egs3/mini_an4/asr/src/app.py egs3/librispeech_100/asr/src/app.py` and `diff egs3/TEMPLATE/asr/src/app.py egs3/librispeech_100/asr/src/app.py` both report no differences (byte-identical files).
findings.suggested_fix: Move build_demo()/main() into espnet3/publication/demo/ (e.g. a launch_gradio_app helper) and have each recipe's src/app.py be a thin wrapper that imports and calls it, keeping only the `if __name__ == '__main__'` entry point recipe-local if needed at all.

findings.summary: build_output_transducer is dead code: it is not referenced by output_fn in any shipped config (mini_an4's transducer config uses src.inference.build_output instead) or by any test, so it is unexercised and can silently rot / mislead a recipe author into thinking it is the sanctioned transducer output formatter.
findings.scenario: A recipe author sees build_output_transducer in TEMPLATE/asr/src/inference.py, assumes it is the correct output_fn to pair with espnet2.bin.asr_transducer_inference.Speech2Text, and sets `output_fn: src.inference.build_output_transducer`. If return_decoded_hyp is left at its default False, Speech2Text.__call__ returns raw Hypothesis objects (not (text, token, token_int, hyp) tuples), so `hyp = model_output[0]` (line 15) yields a Hypothesis object rather than a string, which then gets written into the hyp SCP file as a garbage repr instead of decoded text.
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'build_output_transducer' egs3/ espnet3/ test/ finds only the definition at egs3/TEMPLATE/asr/src/inference.py:12, no callers. mini_an4/asr/conf/inference_transducer.yaml:56 instead sets `output_fn: src.inference.build_output` together with `return_decoded_hyp: true` (line 53), which is the combination that actually produces text via espnet2/bin/asr_transducer_inference.py's hypotheses_to_results() (returns (text, token, token_int, hyp) tuples, matching build_output's `model_output[0][0]` indexing).
findings.suggested_fix: Either delete build_output_transducer if it is truly unneeded, or wire it into mini_an4's inference_transducer.yaml with a comment clarifying it is only correct when return_decoded_hyp is left False, since as written the two output_fn variants in this file are easy to mismatch with return_decoded_hyp.

findings.summary: In the multi-optimizer path, manual_backward(step.loss) deposits gradients into every parameter reachable from that loss, and other optimizers' grads are only zeroed when their own accum_counter is 0, so a mid-accumulation optimizer silently absorbs another loss's gradient.
findings.scenario: Documented GAN setup (g_loss = D(G(x)) backprops through D) with discriminator accum_grad_steps: 2 (or step_every_n_iters: 2). Batch 0: D counter 0 -> zero_grad clears the spurious dg/dD, D grad correct. Batch 1: D counter is 1 so no zero_grad; generator step runs manual_backward(g_loss) which adds dg_loss/dD into D.grad; then d_loss/2 is added and optimizer.step applies grad = d_loss_grad + dg_loss/dD. Verified: D.grad at step == pure d_loss grad -> False; (D.grad - pure) == dg_loss/dD -> True (values [0.625,0.055] vs pure [0.4,0.6]).
findings.evidence: L951-955: `if state.accum_counter == 0: optimizer.zero_grad()` then `self.manual_backward(step.loss / spec.accum_grad_steps)` -- backward is not restricted to the named optimizer's params; L972 zero_grad only after a step. TEMPLATE training.yaml L145-163 documents accum_grad_steps/step_every_n_iters per optimizer for exactly this GAN case.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict the backward to the selected parameters: `self.manual_backward(loss, inputs=self._params_for(step.name))` (torch backward(inputs=...) accumulates only into those leaves), or zero_grad the params of all *other* optimizers before each backward and document that models must detach cross-branch inputs.

findings.summary: step_every_n_iters keeps calling backward on every iteration and only gates optimizer.step, so gradients from N iterations are summed with no 1/N scaling (loss is divided by accum_grad_steps only); the TEMPLATE describes it as 'only step on every N-th training iteration'.
findings.scenario: optimizers.discriminator.step_every_n_iters: 2, accum_grad_steps: 1 (TEMPLATE-style). Batch 0: backward, counter=1, meets_accum True, meets_iter False -> continue (grad kept). Batch 1: backward again, step. Verified: gradient at step / single-batch gradient = [2.22, 1.72] (2x plus the contamination term from the previous finding); effective learning rate is doubled. With step_every_n_iters 3 and accum_grad_steps 2, three micro-batches scaled by 1/2 are applied (1.5x).
findings.evidence: L954 `self.manual_backward(step.loss / spec.accum_grad_steps)`; L958-961 `meets_accum = state.accum_counter >= spec.accum_grad_steps; meets_iter = (batch_idx + 1) % spec.step_every_n_iters == 0; if not (meets_accum and meets_iter): continue` -- the counter is not reset and grads are not dropped on the skipped iterations. TEMPLATE L152-153: 'accum_grad_steps: number of backward passes before optimizer.step()' / 'step_every_n_iters: only step on every N-th training iteration'.
findings.suggested_fix: Either make skipped iterations true no-ops (skip backward for that optimizer when the iteration gate is not met) or scale the loss by 1/(accum_grad_steps*step_every_n_iters) and document that step_every_n_iters accumulates. Add a test asserting gradient magnitude for step_every_n_iters=2.

findings.summary: Top-level `init:` (documented in the TEMPLATE and set to xavier_uniform in all four mini_an4 ASR recipes) is never applied: the trainer reads `init` from config.trainer, and get_espnet_model only forwards `model` so the task's own `args.init` stays None.
findings.scenario: egs3/mini_an4/asr/conf/training_asr_transformer.yaml L127 `init: xavier_uniform` (top-level). training.py L33-37 builds ESPnet3LightningTrainer(config=config.trainer); trainer.py L74 `getattr(self.config, 'init', None)` -> config.trainer has no `init` -> initialize() never called. get_espnet_model (task_utils.py L39-56) merges only config.model into the task defaults, so espnet3/systems/asr/task.py L659 `if args.init is not None` is also False. Result: every mini_an4 model trains with PyTorch default init while the config says xavier_uniform. Conversely, moving `init` under `trainer:` makes `lightning.Trainer(**trainer_config)` (L152-161) raise TypeError because _del_config_key_on does not strip it.
findings.evidence: trainer.py L74-75: `if getattr(self.config, 'init', None) is not None: initialize(self.model, self.config.init)` with self.config = config.trainer (training.py L37). grep for other readers of a top-level `init` in espnet3/: none (only espnet2-style `args.init` inside task.build_model).
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the top-level init explicitly: `ESPnet3LightningTrainer(..., init=config.get('init'))` in training.py and apply it there (before fit so a resumed checkpoint still overrides it), or forward `init` into the model config for the task path. Remove the misleading `init:` entry from the TEMPLATE otherwise.

findings.summary: _sync2skip decides whether to run the NaN-skip collective from config.num_device == 1, which is the per-node device count; with num_nodes > 1 and one device per node each rank decides independently and a NaN on one rank leaves the others blocked in DDP all-reduce.
findings.scenario: TEMPLATE training.yaml L17-18 num_device: 1, num_nodes: 2 (trainer.num_nodes: ${num_nodes}). Rank 0 gets a NaN loss, returns None from training_step (no backward); rank 1 has a finite loss and runs backward -> DDP gradient all-reduce waits forever for rank 0. The same test at L1005-1006 also runs in validation_step, so any per-rank NaN in validation desynchronises ranks too.
findings.evidence: L220-222: `if self.config.num_device == 1: any_invalid = flag_skip else: world_size = torch.distributed.get_world_size(); torch.distributed.barrier(); ...`.
