findings.suggested_fix: Replace DummyOrganizer/DummyDataset with a real espnet3.components.data.dataset.CombinedDataset (as test_data_organizer.py and test_dataloader_builder.py already do) wired through _build_dataset/build_env_local, so the use_espnet_collator flag CollectStatsInferenceProvider actually sets is what governs dataset[i]'s shape; add a case with use_espnet_preprocessor=True + a custom (non-CommonCollateFn) collate_fn and assert on real, non-garbage uids and feature values.

findings.summary: collect_stats() rejects a dataloader config as soon as the mode's config merely HAS a multiple_iterator key (via hasattr), regardless of its value, so explicitly writing `multiple_iterator: false` (e.g. copied/adapted from an ESPnet2 config) raises the same 'ESPnet3 does not support multiple_iterator' RuntimeError as `multiple_iterator: true`.
findings.scenario: A user adapting an ESPnet2-style dataloader config to ESPnet3 keeps an explicit `train: {multiple_iterator: false, ...}` for clarity/documentation. collect_stats() then unconditionally raises RuntimeError even though the value clearly opts out of multiple-iterator mode, because `hasattr(mode_config, 'multiple_iterator')` is true for either boolean value. The identical hasattr-based pattern also exists in espnet3/components/data/dataloader.py:196 for the training dataloader path, so this is a systemic convention, not a one-off typo -- but the error message ('does not support multiple_iterator') reads as if it depends on the value being truthy, which will mislead users debugging the failure.
findings.evidence: collect_stats.py:549-551 `if mode_config is not None and hasattr(mode_config, 'multiple_iterator'): raise RuntimeError("ESPnet3 does not support multiple_iterator. ...")`. Confirmed by test/espnet3/utils/test_dataloader_builder.py::test_multiple_iterator_is_rejected and test/espnet3/components/data/test_collect_stats.py::test_collect_stats_rejects_multiple_iterator, both parametrized `[True, False]` and both expecting the RuntimeError in either case -- i.e. the tests correctly document this behavior as intentional, but neither the tests nor the error message make it clear to a config author that even an explicit `false` is rejected.
findings.suggested_fix: Either check the truthy value (`getattr(mode_config, 'multiple_iterator', False)`) so `multiple_iterator: false` is accepted, or -- if presence-of-key rejection really is intended -- reword the error to say 'the multiple_iterator key is not recognized by ESPnet3 in this location; remove it' rather than implying it depends on the boolean value.

findings.summary: test_ema_moves_ema_model_to_online_device sets up the move_ema_to_online_device branch (via a monkeypatched get_module_device simulating a device mismatch) but only asserts torch.isfinite(ema.ema_model.weight).all(), a property that would hold identically whether or not the move-to-device logic executes at all.
findings.scenario: If EMA.update()'s handling of move_ema_to_online_device were deleted entirely, or the branch that calls .to(device) on the EMA copy were silently skipped, the EMA weights computed on CPU would still be finite floats and the assertion would still pass -- the test does not check ema_model's device, nor compare against a value computed with the move disabled.
findings.evidence: test_ema.py:626-629 `with torch.no_grad(): net.weight.fill_(1.0)\n ema.update()\n assert torch.isfinite(ema.ema_model.weight).all()` -- no assertion on .device, and no differential comparison against the non-move code path.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert ema.ema_model's parameters/buffers end up on the device returned by the (mocked) online-model device sequence, or compare the updated weight against a hand-computed expected value that would only match if the move-then-update ordering is correct.

findings.summary: BaseRunner._run_parallel_dask, the only code path that actually dispatches shards to Dask workers (including its exception/client.cancel(futures) cleanup), is never exercised by any test under test/espnet3/parallel/** or test/espnet3/systems/**.
findings.scenario: Every BaseRunner/InferenceRunner test in scope either passes no `parallel` config (get_parallel_config() returns None) or explicitly sets env='local', both of which route through __call__'s `self._run_local(pending)` branch (base_runner.py:475-478). A regression in _run_parallel_dask -- e.g. the client.cancel(futures) exception-cleanup at base_runner.py:~450-465, or a bug in how worker_setup_fn/env are threaded through wrap_func_with_worker_env -- would ship with the full test suite green.
findings.evidence: grep -rln "_run_parallel_dask" test/espnet3/ espnet3/ only matches espnet3/parallel/base_runner.py itself, never a test file. __call__ dispatch: `if par_config is None or getattr(par_config, 'env', 'local') == 'local': self._run_local(pending) else: self._run_parallel_dask(pending)` (base_runner.py:474-477).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a BaseRunner test that sets parallel.env to a non-'local' value (e.g. 'local_gpu' or a stubbed custom env with n_workers>1) so _plan_shards produces >1 shard and _run_parallel_dask actually runs against a real local Dask client (test_parallel.py already shows how to spin one up), including a case that forces a worker exception to cover the cancel-on-failure path.

findings.summary: BaseRunner._plan_shards silently ignores parallel.n_workers whenever parallel.env=='local', always producing exactly 1 shard, with no warning that the configured worker count was not honoured.
findings.scenario: A recipe author sets `parallel: {env: local, n_workers: 8}` (a plausible config for local multiprocessing during e.g. remove_long_short duration scanning or STFT-style inference) expecting 8-way local parallelism. Every item is instead processed sequentially in one shard on the driver process, silently, with no log line or error indicating n_workers was not used.
findings.evidence: espnet3/parallel/base_runner.py:283-291: `num_shards = 1; if par_config is not None and env not in ("local",): num_shards = int(getattr(par_config, "n_workers", 1))`. Verified live: `set_parallel({'env':'local','n_workers':2}); r._plan_shards(range(10))` -> 1 shard, while `env='local_gpu'` with the same n_workers=2 -> 2 shards.
findings.suggested_fix: Either honour n_workers for env='local' by chunking across a local process/thread pool (matching what the two 'parallel shards' tests in test_inference_runner.py appear to assume), or log a warning when n_workers>1 is configured together with env='local' so the mismatch is visible instead of silent.

findings.summary: test_parallel_shards_offline_with_base_runner and test_parallel_shards_streaming_with_base_runner set n_workers=2/3 with env='local' to claim they test parallel shard dispatch, but env='local' forces exactly 1 shard (see base_runner.py finding above), so the tests only ever exercise the single-shard sequential path and would pass identically with n_workers removed.
findings.scenario: If BaseRunner's multi-shard splitting (_plan_shards for non-local envs) or the Dask dispatch path (_run_parallel_dask) were broken, these two tests would still pass: `shard_dirs = sorted(base.glob('split.*')); assert len(shard_dirs) >= 1` is satisfied trivially by the single shard='split.0' that _run_local always produces under env='local'.
findings.evidence: test_inference_runner.py:291-303 and :325-337 build `OmegaConf.create({'env': 'local', 'n_workers': 2 (or 3), 'options': {...}})` and pass it to set_parallel, then only assert `len(shard_dirs) >= 1` (line 317, 351) rather than `== n_workers` or comparing against the actual configured worker count.
findings.suggested_fix: Either switch these tests to a non-'local' env (with a stubbed/local Dask client) and assert len(shard_dirs) == n_workers to actually cover multi-shard dispatch, or rename/re-scope them as single-shard offline/streaming smoke tests and rely on a separate test (per the test-gap finding above) for real parallel dispatch.

findings.summary: test_materialize_output_value_rejects_top_level_lists is an almost verbatim duplicate of test_inference.py::test_materialize_output_value_rejects_top_level_list (same SUT call with the same arguments, same assertion).
findings.scenario: No missed regression results from this on its own (the behaviour is still covered), but it is dead weight: two files must be kept in sync for one behaviour, and a reviewer scanning test_inference_utils.py could mistake a 14-line, single-test file for a real coverage gap in _materialize_output_value's other branches (audio/text/json/custom-writer artifact types), which are actually only covered in test_inference.py.
findings.evidence: test/espnet3/systems/base/test_inference_utils.py:6-13 calls `_materialize_output_value(idx_value="utt1", field_key="hyp", value=["h1","h2"], output_dir=tmp_path, artifact_config=None)` and expects TypeError match 'Top-level list outputs are not supported'; test/espnet3/systems/base/test_inference.py:338-346 calls the same function with value=["hello"] and the identical assertion.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete one of the two tests (keep the one colocated with the rest of the artifact-materialization tests in test_inference.py), or repurpose test_inference_utils.py to cover other _materialize_output_value branches not exercised elsewhere.

findings.summary: AverageCheckpointsCallback averages a stale top-K set: Lightning reorders every ModelCheckpoint to the END of trainer.callbacks, so on_validation_end averaging runs before this validation's best checkpoint is saved; the final epoch's best ckpt is never averaged and `ave_{K}best.pth` is never written when max_epochs <= K.
findings.scenario: Default TEMPLATE criterion ('valid/loss',3,'min') with max_epochs=3: validations at epochs 0,1,2 -> averaging sees best_k_models of size 0,1,2 -> files valid.loss.ave_1best.pth and valid.loss.ave_2best.pth exist, valid.loss.ave_3best.pth never exists although best_k_models ends with 3 entries. With max_epochs=100 the last ave_3best.pth written excludes the epoch-99 checkpoint even if it is the best, and includes the checkpoint it displaced. egs3/librispeech_100/asr/conf/inference.yaml:61 hardcodes `${exp_dir}/valid.acc.ave_10best.pth` (criterion valid/acc,10,max): missing until the 11th validation, stale by one validation afterwards; mini_an4 (max_epochs=1) never gets an averaged model at all.
findings.evidence: default_callbacks.py:504-511 builds [last_ckpt, *best_ckpts, ave_ckpt, ...]; lightning/pytorch/trainer/connectors/callback_connector.py:240-258 `_reorder_callbacks` moves all `Checkpoint` instances after other callbacks. Verified run (lightning 2.6.1): runtime order = [AverageCheckpointsCallback, LearningRateMonitor, MetricsLogger, TQDMProgressBar, ModelCheckpoint, ModelCheckpoint]; files after 3 epochs = epoch{0,1,2}_*_valid.loss.ckpt, last.ckpt, step12.ckpt, valid.loss.ave_1best.pth, valid.loss.ave_2best.pth (no ave_3best) while best_k_models has 3 entries. L125 reads `ckpt_callback.best_k_models` before ModelCheckpoint.on_validation_end updates it.
findings.suggested_fix: Make AverageCheckpointsCallback a `Checkpoint` subclass placed after the ModelCheckpoints (so it is reordered with them, order preserved), or perform the averaging in `on_train_epoch_end`/`on_fit_end` after checkpoints are saved, or average on demand in the infer stage from ModelCheckpoint.best_k_models. Also write to a stable name (e.g. `{monitor}.ave_best.pth`) or delete stale `ave_{k}best.pth` files.

findings.summary: With EMACallback enabled, the best-K checkpoints are selected by a metric computed on EMA weights but store the ONLINE weights and contain no EMA state: EMACallback.on_validation_end (restore) runs before ModelCheckpoint.on_validation_end (save) because Lightning moves checkpoints to the end, and best ckpts use save_weights_only=True which skips callbacks' on_save_checkpoint.
findings.scenario: trainer.callbacks: [{_target_: espnet3.components.callbacks.ema.EMACallback}] with the default best_model_criterion. Validation runs on EMA weights (swap in on_validation_start), valid/loss is logged for EMA weights; EMACallback.on_validation_end restores online weights; then ModelCheckpoint saves `epochN_stepM_valid.loss.ckpt` from `pl_module.state_dict()` = online weights. The infer stage / AverageCheckpointsCallback therefore load models that never produced the monitored score; the EMA weights exist only inside last.ckpt (`ema_model_state_dict`), which inference does not read.
findings.evidence: Verified run: runtime order [..., EMACallback, ModelCheckpoint, ModelCheckpoint]; best ckpt keys = ['epoch','global_step','loops','pytorch-lightning_version','state_dict'] (no ema_model_state_dict); last.ckpt has ema_model_state_dict. lightning checkpoint_connector.py dump_checkpoint: `if not weights_only: call._call_callbacks_on_save_checkpoint(...)`; default_callbacks.py:490 `save_weights_only=True`. ema.py:134-136 restores in on_validation_end; ema.py:146-149 only writes EMA state via on_save_checkpoint.
findings.suggested_fix: Either keep EMA weights swapped in until after the checkpoint callbacks run (e.g. restore in `on_train_epoch_end`/`on_validation_epoch_end` is too early too; make EMACallback a `Checkpoint` subclass placed after the ModelCheckpoints, or restore in `on_train_batch_start`), or save the EMA weights as the model `state_dict` when EMA is active, or set save_weights_only=False so `ema_model_state_dict` is included and teach inference to prefer it. Document the current semantics at minimum.

findings.summary: Default callbacks (last/best ModelCheckpoint, AverageCheckpoints, LearningRateMonitor, MetricsLogger, TQDMProgressBar) are hard-wired and cannot be disabled or replaced, so ordinary Lightning trainer options crash at startup with messages that do not mention ESPnet3's defaults; user callbacks are only appended (duplicates allowed).
findings.scenario: trainer.logger: false (or any config without loggers) -> `MisconfigurationException: Cannot use LearningRateMonitor callback with Trainer that has no logger.` at on_train_start. trainer.enable_progress_bar: false (typical for batch jobs) -> `MisconfigurationException: Trainer was configured with enable_progress_bar=False but found TQDMProgressBar in callbacks list.` trainer.enable_checkpointing: false -> same class of error for ModelCheckpoint. Adding a ModelCheckpoint/LearningRateMonitor via trainer.callbacks yields two instances (codified in test_duplicate_learning_rate_monitor_from_config).
findings.evidence: trainer.py:96-106 always calls get_default_callbacks and appends config callbacks; default_callbacks.py:499,502,504-511. Verified run: logger=False raised the LearningRateMonitor MisconfigurationException; enable_progress_bar=False raised the TQDMProgressBar MisconfigurationException (lightning callback_connector.py:148, lr_monitor.py:121-124). Note: lightning treats logger=None as no logger (`configure_logger`: `if not logger`), yet test_logger_variants asserts a TensorBoardLogger for None, so behaviour with `logger:` unset should be re-checked.
findings.suggested_fix: Build defaults conditionally (skip LearningRateMonitor when no logger, skip TQDMProgressBar when enable_progress_bar is False, skip checkpoint callbacks when enable_checkpointing is False), and/or expose per-callback switches in the trainer config; de-duplicate by type when merging user callbacks.

findings.summary: The documented top-level `init:` key ('forwarded to ESPnet's initializer', e.g. xavier_uniform) is never read: trainer.py looks for `init` inside the `trainer` block only, and if a user moves it there the un-stripped key is forwarded to lightning.Trainer and raises TypeError.
findings.scenario: User sets top-level `init: xavier_uniform` as the template suggests -> training.py:37 passes config=config.trainer, trainer.py:74 `getattr(self.config, 'init')` is None -> no initialization, silently different training. User sets `trainer.init: xavier_uniform` -> initialize() runs but `init` stays in trainer_config (not in the deletion list at trainer.py:141-148) -> `lightning.Trainer(init=...)` TypeError: unexpected keyword argument.
findings.evidence: training.yaml:202-204; training.py:34-39 (`config=config.trainer`); trainer.py:74-75 and 141-149. grep for other consumers of `.init`/`initialize(` in espnet3/: only trainer.py (transducer_task.py uses espnet2 argparse `args.init`).
findings.suggested_fix: Read `init` from the full training config (pass it explicitly to ESPnet3LightningTrainer from training.py) or move the documented key under `trainer:` and add 'init' to the stripped-key list.

findings.summary: The train stage has no resume/ckpt_path discovery (`fit: {}` by default); re-running `--stages train` in the same exp_dir silently starts from scratch and, because the last-checkpoint callback uses the version counter, produces `last-v1.ckpt` while `last.ckpt` keeps pointing at the previous run; `last-v1.ckpt` also escapes publication.yaml's `last.ckpt` exclude pattern.
findings.scenario: Training crashes (OOM/preemption) and the user re-runs `python run.py --stages train ...`. No ckpt_path is passed -> training restarts at epoch 0; ModelCheckpoint(save_last='link') finds an existing last.ckpt whose path != self.last_model_path ('' on a fresh run) -> writes last-v1.ckpt; old step*.ckpt / best ckpts from the first run remain next to the new ones. pack_model bulk copy excludes only `last.ckpt` and `**/step*.ckpt`, so the multi-GB `last-v1.ckpt` (optimizer states included) is packed.
findings.evidence: training.py:96-100 (`fit_kwargs` only from config.fit; no ckpt_path logic anywhere in espnet3/, grep 'ckpt_path|last.ckpt|resume' has no hits outside comments); default_callbacks.py:467-474 (save_last='link', default enable_version_counter=True); lightning model_checkpoint.py:912-916. Verified run: second fit() into the same exp_dir left ['epoch0..2 ckpts','last-v1.ckpt','last.ckpt','step12.ckpt','step4.ckpt'] with last.ckpt -> step12.ckpt (old run). egs3/TEMPLATE/asr/conf/publication.yaml:69-73 exclude list.
findings.suggested_fix: Default `ckpt_path='last'` when exp_dir/last.ckpt exists (Lightning resolves 'last' from ModelCheckpoint dirpaths and warns if none), or refuse to train into a non-empty exp_dir without an explicit flag; set enable_version_counter=False on the last-ckpt callback; broaden the publication exclude to `last*.ckpt`.

findings.summary: `reload_dataloaders_every_n_epochs=1` and `use_distributed_sampler=False` are only forced for the espnet iter_factory path, but DataLoaderBuilder's epoch/rank shard rotation (total_shards/dist_world_size) applies to the standard-DataLoader path too, so a sharded standard dataloader never rotates shards and is additionally subsampled by Lightning's DistributedSampler.
findings.scenario: dataloader.train without an `iter_factory` key but with total_shards: 4, dist_world_size: 2 (the keys sit next to iter_factory in the template and survive a switch to a plain DataLoader). trainer.py:113 hasattr(...,'iter_factory') is False -> reload stays at Lightning default 0 -> train_dataloader() is built once with epoch=0 -> shard_idx=(0*2+rank)%4 forever; is_espnet_sampler False -> use_distributed_sampler stays True -> each rank's shard is further split r::world_size, so each epoch consumes 1/world_size of the assigned shard and shards 2,3 are never seen.
findings.evidence: trainer.py:113-133 (`if hasattr(self.model.config.dataloader.train, 'iter_factory')` guards the override), 137-138; espnet3/components/data/dataloader.py:140-141 `shard_idx = ((self.epoch * runtime_world_size) + rank) % total_shards; return dataset.shard(shard_idx)` executed in build() for both branches (dataloader.py:197-217); lightning_module.py:1145-1152 passes `epoch=self.current_epoch`.
findings.suggested_fix: Force reload_dataloaders_every_n_epochs=1 (and use_distributed_sampler=False) whenever total_shards is configured, independent of iter_factory; or make _maybe_shard_dataset assert the trainer settings it needs.

findings.summary: All AverageCheckpointsCallback and EMACallback tests drive hooks by hand on mocks/SimpleNamespace trainers; nothing exercises a real lightning.Trainer, so the hook-ordering defects (stale top-K averaging, best ckpts holding online weights, missing ave_{K}best.pth) are invisible, and one test codifies callback duplication as expected behaviour.
findings.scenario: test_average_checkpoints_callback_on_validation_end patches torch.load/torch.save and injects best_k_models directly; test_ema.py::_make_trainer is a SimpleNamespace; test_logging_callback.py calls the non-existent hook `on_after_optimizer_step` directly and its header table (lines 12-18) describes load_line tests copied from another file. A 3-epoch CPU run with get_default_callbacks would have caught the ave_3best.pth absence.
findings.evidence: test_callback.py:76-78 mock.patch('torch.load'), :84-88 mock.Mock(best_k_models=...); test_ema.py:247-252 SimpleNamespace trainer; test_logging_callback.py:52 `callback.on_after_optimizer_step(trainer, model)`; test_callback.py:386-414 asserts two LearningRateMonitor instances 'because no deduplication or warning is implemented yet'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one small end-to-end test (tiny LightningModule, 3 epochs, CSVLogger) asserting the averaged file set, that the best ckpt state_dict equals the weights that produced the monitored metric with EMA on, and the runtime callback order; fix the copied header table.

findings.summary: MetricsLogger.on_after_optimizer_step is not a Lightning Callback hook, so `optim_step_time` is never recorded (dead code) while the docstring/log format imply it is reported.
findings.scenario: Any training run: Lightning calls on_before_optimizer_step (starts the timer) but never on_after_optimizer_step; `_sum['optim_step_time']` is never populated, and the summary line lists iter_time/forward_time/backward_time/train_time only. test_logging_callback.py:52 calls the method manually, hiding the gap.
findings.evidence: grep -rn on_after_optimizer_step over lightning/pytorch (2.6.1): no hits; only default_callbacks.py:299 defines it. Lightning's Callback exposes on_before_optimizer_step/on_before_zero_grad only.
findings.suggested_fix: Measure the optimizer step in `on_before_zero_grad` (called right after optimizer.step in automatic optimization) or drop the metric; in the manual path call the timer from the LightningModule.

findings.summary: The use_distributed_sampler warning is dead/inverted: it tests `hasattr(self.model.config, 'use_distributed_sampler')` (the full training config, where the key never lives) but reads `self.config.use_distributed_sampler` (trainer block), and warns when the value is ALREADY False (`not ...`); both warning strings also lack a space ('to setreload_dataloaders_every_n_epochs').
findings.scenario: trainer.use_distributed_sampler: true with an espnet iter_factory -> no warning (hasattr on model.config is False); the value is then silently overridden to False at line 138. If a user put use_distributed_sampler at the top level and False in trainer, the warning fires although the value is already correct.
findings.evidence: trainer.py:123-131 vs :137-138; message strings :118-121, :127-130.
findings.suggested_fix: Check `getattr(self.config, 'use_distributed_sampler', None) is True` and warn about the override; fix the strings.

findings.summary: ESPnet3LightningTrainer advertises `config: Union[DictConfig, Namespace, Dict[str, Any]]` but uses attribute access and attribute assignment on it, so a plain dict fails with AttributeError; it also mutates the caller's shared trainer config in place before deep-copying.
findings.scenario: ESPnet3LightningTrainer(model=lit, exp_dir='exp', config={'max_epochs': 1, 'log_every_n_steps': 10}) -> `self.config.log_every_n_steps` AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'log_every_n_steps'; with an espnet sampler `self.config.reload_dataloaders_every_n_epochs = 1` would also fail. With a DictConfig the assignment at :133/:138 changes `training_config.trainer` for the rest of the process (stages share one config).
findings.evidence: trainer.py:51 type hint; :98 `self.config.log_every_n_steps`; :133 `self.config.reload_dataloaders_every_n_epochs = 1`; :138 `self.config.use_distributed_sampler = False`; :140 deepcopy happens after the mutation.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalise `config` to a DictConfig (OmegaConf.create) at the top of __init__ and operate on a private copy; or narrow the type hint.

findings.summary: `trainer.log_every_n_steps` is silently mandatory: when the key is absent the DictConfig yields None and get_default_callbacks' typeguard rejects it with 'argument log_interval (None) is not an instance of int', although Lightning itself defaults the option to 50 and the template does not mark it required.
findings.scenario: A recipe trainer block copied from Lightning docs without log_every_n_steps -> TypeCheckError from typeguard at trainer construction, pointing at get_default_callbacks rather than at the missing config key.
findings.evidence: trainer.py:98 `self.config.log_every_n_steps` (no default); default_callbacks.py:424-430 `@typechecked ... log_interval: int = 500`.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `getattr(self.config, 'log_every_n_steps', 50)` or validate required trainer keys with an explicit error message.

findings.summary: EMACallback creates the EMA copy only for stage == 'fit', so trainer.validate()/trainer.test() with a checkpoint never swap EMA weights in (and on_load_checkpoint skips the saved EMA state), contrary to the class docstring 'Swaps EMA weights in for validation/test'.
findings.scenario: `trainer.validate(ckpt_path='exp/last.ckpt')` after an EMA run: setup(stage='validate') leaves self.ema None -> on_load_checkpoint ignores `ema_model_state_dict` -> _swap_in_ema returns early -> metrics are computed on online weights, silently different from the numbers logged during training.
findings.evidence: ema.py:56 `if stage == 'fit' and trainer.is_global_zero`; ema.py:153 `if 'ema_model_state_dict' in checkpoint and self.ema is not None`; docstring ema.py:13-18. test_ema.py::test_callback_setup_skips_other_stage_or_rank codifies the behaviour.
findings.suggested_fix: Create the EMA holder for validate/test too when a checkpoint provides `ema_model_state_dict`, or narrow the docstring.

findings.summary: The 'integer-type not averaged' guard uses `str(dtype).startswith('torch.int')`, which misses torch.uint8 and torch.bool buffers; those are summed and divided into float tensors before being saved in the averaged state_dict.
findings.scenario: A model with a `torch.bool` mask buffer that is True in one of three checkpoints: sum -> bool OR -> True, then `/3` -> float 0.333 saved; load_state_dict copies back to bool as True. For a uint8 lookup buffer the averaged float is truncated on load. Edge case; bf16/fp16 weights are also averaged in their own low precision (sum of K values before division).
findings.evidence: default_callbacks.py:157 `if str(avg_state_dict[k].dtype).startswith('torch.int')`; :154 accumulation `avg_state_dict[k] + state_dict[k]`; :169 division.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `not (torch.is_floating_point(t) or torch.is_complex(t))` as the guard and accumulate floats in float32 before casting back.

findings.summary: MetricsLogger's `iter_time` spans validation, checkpointing and the per-epoch dataloader rebuild because `_last_batch_end_time` is never cleared by `_reset()`; the first batch of every epoch (and every log window that follows validation) reports an inflated iter_time.
findings.scenario: reload_dataloaders_every_n_epochs=1 (forced for espnet iter_factory) + validation + checkpoint averaging at epoch end take e.g. 90 s; the next epoch's first on_train_batch_start adds 90 s to `_sum['iter_time']`, so the first '1-100batch' line shows iter_time~0.9 s instead of ~1 ms and the epoch_summary iter_time is skewed.
findings.evidence: default_callbacks.py:275-277 uses `t - self._last_batch_end_time`; `_reset()` (256-264) and `_reset_epoch()` (266-269) do not touch `_last_batch_end_time`; it is set at :342 on every batch end.
findings.suggested_fix: Reset `_last_batch_end_time` in on_train_epoch_start/on_validation_end, or compute iter_time only within an epoch.

findings.summary: AverageCheckpointsCallback re-loads and re-averages every top-K checkpoint from disk on every validation (including the resume sanity-check validation) and writes a differently named file for every K seen, leaving stale `ave_1best`..`ave_{K-1}best` files and failing hard if a restored best_k_models path no longer exists.
findings.scenario: K=10 large models: 10 full checkpoint loads per epoch on rank 0 while other ranks wait at the next barrier. Resume after moving/cleaning exp_dir: best_k_models (restored from last.ckpt callback state) points at deleted files -> safe_torch_load FileNotFoundError during the sanity check. Old ave_{k}best.pth files never removed; a consumer that picks the wrong K silently loads an older average.
findings.evidence: default_callbacks.py:120-132 loop over all best_k_models each on_validation_end; no `trainer.sanity_checking` guard; :195-199 filename with `len(checkpoints)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip during sanity_checking, average only when best_k_models changed (compare the key set), use a fixed filename, and tolerate/skip missing paths with a warning.

findings.summary: TTSSystem.collect_stats leaves model.normalize untouched, so every espnet2-canonical TTS config (normalize: global_mvn with normalize_conf.stats_file under stats_dir) crashes on the first collect_stats run with FileNotFoundError, i.e. the chicken-and-egg the docstring claims to solve is only solved for `normalize: null` configs.
findings.scenario: training_config.task=espnet2.tasks.tts.TTSTask, model.normalize=global_mvn, model.normalize_conf.stats_file=${stats_dir}/train/feats_stats.npz (the shipped egs2 VITS/Tacotron2/FastSpeech2 shape), stats_dir empty -> TTSSystem.collect_stats() -> _build_trainer -> get_espnet_model -> TTSTask.build_model -> GlobalMVN(stats_file=...) -> np.load -> FileNotFoundError: 'exp/stats/train/feats_stats.npz' before any stats are collected. Same for pitch_normalize/energy_normalize (FastSpeech2). The base path (pop) fails too (TypeError missing stats_file); espnet2 tts.sh avoids both by passing --normalize none --pitch_normalize none --energy_normalize none to collect_stats. On a later re-run, stale stats from a previous collection are silently loaded instead.
findings.evidence: system.py:496-498 `# Build the trainer WITHOUT popping normalize/normalize_conf ... trainer = _build_trainer(self.training_config)`; espnet2/tasks/tts.py:307-309 `normalize_class = normalize_choices.get_class(args.normalize); normalize = normalize_class(**args.normalize_conf)`; espnet2/layers/global_mvn.py:37-40 `stats = np.load(stats_file)`; egs2/TEMPLATE/tts1/tts.sh:733-735 `--normalize none --pitch_normalize none --energy_normalize none`. Repro (SCRATCH/tts/repro_normalize.py): A: keys kept + global_mvn -> `FileNotFoundError [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'exp/stats/train/feats_stats.npz'`; B: keys popped -> `TypeError GlobalMVN.__init__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'stats_file'`; C/D: normalize=None -> OK.
findings.suggested_fix: In collect_stats build the model from a deep copy of the config with model.normalize (and pitch_normalize/energy_normalize when present) explicitly set to None (not popped), mirroring espnet2 tts.sh; ideally do this once in base training.collect_stats so ASR and TTS share one correct behaviour and the TTS override disappears.

findings.summary: Base collect_stats pops model.normalize/normalize_conf from the shared training_config in place, so a `train` stage executed in the same invocation silently trains with the task-default normalizer instead of the configured one.
findings.scenario: egs3/TEMPLATE/asr/run.py DEFAULT_STAGES runs collect_stats then train on the same BaseSystem/ASRSystem object. With model.normalize=global_mvn, normalize_conf.stats_file=... : collect_stats pops both keys from self.training_config.model; train() then calls _build_trainer(self.training_config) with model lacking normalize -> ASR task default utterance_mvn is built and save_espnet_config writes config.yaml with the default, so the divergence is invisible afterwards. TTS is unaffected only because TTSSystem overrides collect_stats without the pop.
findings.evidence: training.py:62-65 `if "normalize" in config.model: config.model.pop("normalize")` operating on the caller's DictConfig (system.py:294 passes self.training_config); stages_utils.py:138-184 loops `fn()` over stages on one system; repro output: `before: {'normalize': 'global_mvn', 'normalize_conf': {...}}` / `after collect_stats (what a subsequent train() in the same run sees): {}`; espnet3/systems/asr/task.py:124-131 default="utterance_mvn".
findings.suggested_fix: Operate on `copy.deepcopy(config)` (or OmegaConf.create(OmegaConf.to_container(config))) inside collect_stats and set normalize to None on the copy rather than mutating the shared config.

findings.summary: create_token_list's default path indexes parts[2] without checking column count, so a blank line or a row with fewer than three tab-separated fields crashes with a bare IndexError, while the sibling vocab_builder branch and remove_long_short._load_entries both tolerate exactly those rows.
findings.scenario:
Manifest `u1	/x.wav	ab	spk

u2	/y.wav	cd	spk
` (blank line, which remove_long_short on the same file skips silently) -> create_token_list() -> `IndexError: list index out of range` with no file/line context. Also `u2	/y.wav	
` (empty text, no speaker column): `line.rstrip()` eats the trailing tab so parts has 2 fields -> IndexError, whereas _load_entries treats it as an empty-text drop.
findings.evidence: system.py:365-367 `line = line.rstrip(); parts = line.split("\t"); text = parts[2]`; contrast system.py:308-310 `if len(parts) > 2 and parts[2].strip()` and provider.py:102-108 `stripped = line.rstrip("\n"); if not stripped: continue; if len(parts) < 3 ...`. Repro sections 1/1b: `EXC IndexError list index out of range` for both manifests; 1c shows _load_entries accepts them.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse RemoveLongShortProvider._load_entries (or the same guard) to read the text column, and use rstrip("\n") instead of rstrip().

findings.summary: TTSSystem.__init__ takes **kwargs but also passes a hard-coded stage_log_mapping to BaseSystem, so any caller supplying stage_log_mapping (supported and merged by ASRSystem) gets a TypeError; the constructor signature, type hints and merge semantics diverge from ASRSystem/BaseSystem.
findings.scenario: TTSSystem(training_config=cfg, stage_log_mapping={"infer": "training_config.exp_dir"}) -> `TypeError: BaseSystem.__init__() got multiple values for keyword argument 'stage_log_mapping'`; the identical call on ASRSystem succeeds and merges. Only reachable from custom runners/subclasses (egs3/TEMPLATE/asr/run.py does not pass stage_log_mapping), so this is a misuse path, but the BaseSystem docstring advertises the override.
findings.evidence: system.py:46 `**kwargs,` and :53-57 `stage_log_mapping={...}, **kwargs` vs asr/system.py:60-63 `stage_log_mapping={"train_tokenizer": ..., **(stage_log_mapping or {})}`. Repro section 2: `ASR OK` / `TTS EXC TypeError ... multiple values for keyword argument 'stage_log_mapping'`.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror ASRSystem: accept explicit publication_config/stage_log_mapping/demo_config parameters with type hints and merge the caller's mapping over the TTS defaults.

findings.summary: remove_long_short hard-codes resume=False but never clears the previous shard directory, so a run killed hard (SIGKILL/OOM/SLURM time limit/Dask worker death) leaves split.N/lock behind and every subsequent re-run of the stage fails with a misleading 'already locked by another runner' error until the user manually deletes the lock.
findings.scenario: First run OK. Simulate a hard kill by leaving save_path/shards/train/split.0/lock in place (this is exactly the state after a worker or driver dies inside _run_one_shard, whose finally-unlock never executes) -> TTSSystem.remove_long_short() -> `RuntimeError: Shard is already locked by another runner: .../shards/train/split.0`. The message neither mentions the lock file nor that the stage is safe to restart; with resume=False the whole shard is recomputed anyway so the lock buys nothing.
findings.evidence: system.py:174-180 `RemoveLongShortRunner(..., output_dir=save_path / "shards", shard_subdir=split, resume=False)`; base_runner.py:347-351 `if not self._try_lock_shard(shard_dir): ... raise RuntimeError("Shard is already locked by another runner: " ...)`; base_runner.py:393-394 unlock only in the worker-side finally. Repro section 4: `first run OK` then `rerun EXC RuntimeError Shard is already locked by another runner`.
findings.suggested_fix: Since resume=False, remove (shutil.rmtree) `save_path/shards/<split>` before constructing the runner, or teach BaseRunner to treat locks as stale when resume=False / when the recorded pid is dead, and include the lock path and recovery instruction in the error.

findings.summary: The filtered manifests written by remove_long_short are not consumed by any espnet3 code or config key; create_token_list defaults to the unfiltered data/manifest/train.tsv and the dataset/DataOrganizer must be re-pointed by hand, so a config that enables remove_long_short can still train on unfiltered data with no warning.
findings.scenario: Recipe sets remove_long_short.save_path=data/manifest_filtered and runs the stage; dataset.train[].data_src_args still reference the recipe Dataset's default manifest (data/manifest/train.tsv) and create_token_list.manifest_path is left at its default -> the token list and training set silently include the utterances the stage just removed. Nothing in espnet3/ or egs3/ reads remove_long_short.save_path (grep: only the stage_log_mapping does), and the two TTS stages do not chain to each other by default.
findings.evidence: system.py:147 default `f"data/manifest/{split}.tsv"`, :149 `filtered_manifest_path = save_path / manifest_path.name`, :285 create_token_list default `"data/manifest/train.tsv"`; grep -rn remove_long_short across espnet3/egs3 shows no consumer besides system.py:54 (stage log dir). BaseSystem.create_dataset (base/system.py:249-272) has no hook for post-filtering either.
findings.suggested_fix: Either make the filtered dir the single source of truth (e.g. create_token_list default manifest under remove_long_short.save_path and document that dataset entries must point there) or have the stage emit a keep-list (utt ids) that the DataOrganizer/preprocessor applies, and log a warning when a later stage reads a manifest that has a filtered sibling.

findings.summary: Optional keys are read with DictConfig.get(key, default), which returns None for an explicit `null`, so TEMPLATE-style null placeholders (the convention TEMPLATE/tts/training.yaml documents) for splits / token_type / add_symbol / cutoff crash with TypeError or TypeCheckError instead of falling back to the defaults.
findings.scenario: remove_long_short: {save_path: ..., min_wav_duration: 1, max_wav_duration: 4, splits: null} -> `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable` at `for split in splits`. create_token_list: {..., token_type: null} -> `TypeCheckError: argument "token_type" (None) is not an instance of str`; add_symbol: null -> `None + ...` TypeError at line 388; cutoff: null -> `x[1] > None` TypeError at line 377. The same header says 'Everything ... is left null for the recipe config to fill in', so a recipe author who scaffolds these sections with nulls hits this. Hypothetical config, no shipped TTS recipe.
findings.evidence: system.py:128 `splits = remove_long_short_config.get("splits", ["train", "valid", "test"])`, :333 `.get("token_type", "char")`, :344-347 `.get("add_symbol", [])`, `.get("cutoff", 0)`; TEMPLATE/tts/conf/training.yaml:12-13. Repro section 3: `splits:null EXC TypeError 'NoneType' object is not iterable`; `nulls EXC TypeCheckError argument "token_type" (None) is not an instance of str`.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize `None` to the default for optional keys (e.g. a small helper `cfg.get(k) if cfg.get(k) is not None else default`) and validate types up front with clear messages.

findings.summary: min_wav_duration/max_wav_duration are not validated (min < max, non-negative, numeric); an inverted pair drops every utterance and silently writes empty filtered manifests.
findings.scenario: remove_long_short: {min_wav_duration: 10, max_wav_duration: 1} -> stage completes 'successfully', filtered train.tsv is 0 bytes (only the INFO line 'kept 0' hints at it); downstream stages then fail obscurely on an empty dataset. A string value like '2.0' would instead raise a TypeError inside the worker.
findings.evidence: system.py:115-120 only checks presence via _get_required_config; runner.py:66 `keep = not (duration <= min_duration or duration >= max_duration)`. Repro section 5: `filtered bytes: 0`.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate `0 <= min < max` and numeric types before starting, and raise (or at least warn) when a split ends with zero kept entries.

findings.summary: Filtered output is named after the input manifest's basename, so manifest_paths entries with the same filename in different directories silently overwrite each other.
findings.scenario: manifest_paths: {train: A/manifest.tsv, valid: B/manifest.tsv} -> both splits write save_path/manifest.tsv; the valid pass overwrites the train pass and the log still reports both as saved. Config-dependent misuse; the documented default (data/manifest/{split}.tsv) does not collide.
findings.evidence: system.py:149 `filtered_manifest_path = save_path / manifest_path.name`. Repro section 6: `['manifest.tsv', 'shards'] -> validutt`.
findings.suggested_fix: Name outputs by split (`save_path / f"{split}.tsv"`) or detect duplicate basenames and raise.

findings.summary: One missing or unreadable wav aborts the whole split (and the whole stage) with a raw soundfile error that does not identify the utt_id or manifest line, and there is no option to skip/report bad rows.
findings.scenario: valid.tsv contains one row whose wav path does not exist -> remove_long_short() raises `soundfile.LibsndfileError: Error opening '/no/such.wav': System error.`; the user has to grep the manifest for the path to find the offending utterance, and in Dask mode the error surfaces via future.result() after other shards already ran.
findings.evidence: runner.py:62-63 `utt_id, wav_path, _ = entries[idx]; duration = sf.info(wav_path).duration` with no try/except; repro section 7: `EXC LibsndfileError Error opening '/no/such.wav': System error.`
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap sf.info in try/except, re-raise with utt_id/manifest context, or record keep=False plus an error field and report the count in the summary log.

findings.summary: The docstring says durations are checked 'in parallel', but with the TEMPLATE default parallel.env=local BaseRunner plans exactly one shard and runs sequentially on the driver regardless of n_workers, and in non-local mode a fresh Dask cluster is created and torn down once per split.
findings.scenario: parallel: {env: local, n_workers: 8} -> _plan_shards returns 1 shard (num_shards forced to 1 for env local) and __call__ dispatches to _run_local: all wav headers are read serially. parallel: {env: slurm, n_workers: 8} with splits [train, valid, test] -> three separate get_client() cluster lifecycles.
findings.evidence: system.py:65-66 'in parallel, via RemoveLongShortProvider/Runner'; base_runner.py:286-289 `if par_config is not None and env not in ("local",): num_shards = ...`, :475-478 env==local -> _run_local; system.py:142-188 constructs and calls a new runner per split.
findings.suggested_fix: Document that env=local is sequential (or use a LocalCluster when n_workers>1), and consider processing all splits under one runner/cluster.

findings.summary: TTS TEMPLATE places stats under ${exp_dir}/stats while the ASR TEMPLATE uses ${recipe_dir}/exp/stats, so the two systems disagree on whether stats are per-experiment or shared per recipe.
findings.scenario: A user copying an ASR recipe's habit of running collect_stats once (conf/train_a.yaml) and training several configs (conf/train_b.yaml, ...) gets `${stats_dir}/train/feats_shape` missing under TTS because exp_tag=${self_name:} makes stats_dir depend on the config file name; conversely an ASR user changing frontend settings silently reuses stale shared stats.
findings.evidence: egs3/TEMPLATE/tts/conf/training.yaml:27-29 `exp_tag: ${self_name:} ... stats_dir: ${exp_dir}/stats` vs egs3/TEMPLATE/asr/conf/training.yaml:27-29 `stats_dir: ${recipe_dir}/exp/stats`.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one convention (per-experiment is safer) and apply it to both templates with a comment explaining it.

findings.summary: add_nonsplit_symbol both configures the tokenizer to emit the symbol (so it is counted from the text) and unconditionally inserts it again, producing a duplicate entry in tokens.txt that TokenIDConverter rejects at training time; inherited verbatim from espnet2 tokenize_text but advertised in the espnet3 docstring and untested.
findings.scenario: Manifest text `ab<sc>cd`, create_token_list with add_symbol [<blank>:0, <unk>:1] and add_nonsplit_symbol [<sc>:2] -> tokens.txt = [<blank>, <unk>, <sc>, a, b, <sc>, c, d]; TokenIDConverter(token_list) -> `RuntimeError: Symbol "<sc>" is duplicated` when the preprocessor is built for training.
findings.evidence: system.py:350-359 passes `nonsplit_symbol=add_nonsplit_symbol` to build_tokenizer (char_tokenizer.py:33-37 strips ':idx' and emits the symbol as a token), then :388-401 inserts every add_nonsplit_symbol entry again. Repro section 9 output `['<blank>', '<unk>', '<sc>', 'a', 'b', '<sc>', 'c', 'd']`; TokenIDConverter on that list -> `RuntimeError Symbol "<sc>" is duplicated`.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop nonsplit symbols from `counter` before inserting them (or skip the insert when already present), and add a test.

findings.summary: The TTS TEMPLATE has no remove_long_short / create_token_list sections and no run.py, so the two TTS-specific stages that TTSSystem exists for are in no stage list, have no config scaffold, and their stage_log_mapping entries silently fall back to exp_dir.
findings.scenario: A recipe author starting from egs3/TEMPLATE/tts must write their own runner (egs3/TEMPLATE/asr/run.py DEFAULT_STAGES has no remove_long_short/create_token_list and hard-codes ASR stage names in the guardrail dict) and invent the remove_long_short/create_token_list sections from the docstrings; TTSSystem.__init__ resolves 'training_config.remove_long_short.save_path' to None for the template and logs land in exp_dir instead of the documented save_path.
findings.evidence: training.yaml lines 15-91 contain no remove_long_short/create_token_list keys; `ls egs3/TEMPLATE/tts` = __init__.py, conf/ only; system.py:53-56 stage_log_mapping refers to those keys; base/system.py:147-150 skips unresolved refs; asr/run.py:27-38 DEFAULT_STAGES and :185-201 required_configs.
findings.suggested_fix: Add commented remove_long_short/create_token_list sections to the template and a TTS run.py (or make the shared runner's stage list system-driven).

findings.summary: The collect_stats tests replace _build_trainer with a recorder and assert only that model.normalize 'survives' into the trainer config, which pins the exact behaviour that crashes for global_mvn configs, and nothing exercises TTSSystem end to end (run_stages + TEMPLATE merge), Dask mode, zero-length/missing wavs, stale locks, or a real TTS task model.
findings.scenario: test_collect_stats_preserves_null_normalize passes while a real config with normalize: global_mvn fails in _build_trainer (finding 1); no test covers a manifest whose wav is missing/0 s, a leftover lock, min>=max, blank manifest lines in create_token_list, add_nonsplit_symbol, or a non-local parallel env; there is no TTS recipe in egs3 to catch config/code drift.
findings.evidence: test_system.py:262-280 `monkeypatch.setattr(sysmod, "_build_trainer", fake_build_trainer)`; :294-309 asserts `model_cfg.normalize is None` only; test_remove_long_short.py:53-66 fixture uses 0.5/2/5 s wavs only; grep shows no other TTS tests and no egs3/*/tts recipe.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a collect_stats test against a real (tiny) espnet2 TTS task config with normalize: global_mvn and an empty stats_dir, plus tests for blank manifest lines, missing wav, stale lock, min>=max and a two-shard (non-local) plan via a fake parallel config.
